It clarifies for us the reason for her coming to the trunk of the palm tree, because when the time of a woman's delivery comes she needs something to lean on and to cling to, to ease the pain of labour, or a companion to whom she can turn for help and who shares this suffering with her. So the pains drove her to the trunk of the (palm) tree, and the palm tree came in the definite form because it was a known, familiar palm tree.

The trunk of the palm tree is its stem, which runs from the root to the beginning of the fronds. Will Maryam, at her delivery, cling to this entire stem? Of course not; she will take only the part near her. The word "trunk" is used here in a hyperbolic manner, as in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿They put their fingers into their ears because of the thunderbolts, for fear of death﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

It is well known that a person plugs his ears with the tips of his fingers, not with all of his fingers, so the meaning is expressed by "fingers" in hyperbole, to emphasize blocking out the disturbing sound and the thunderbolts that descend upon them.

Thus Lady Maryam found herself faced with a fait accompli and an evident pregnancy that she could neither conceal nor hide. She had previously accepted that the angel would give her the good news of a pure boy, and she accepted that she would conceive him. So how would she be now, when the matter has passed from words to actual reality, and here is the child in her womb, and the time of his birth has come?

An emotional outburst must have overtaken her, one that went beyond the bounds of concealment and secrecy, and so she says:

﴿O, would that I had died before this, and had become a thing forgotten!﴾ (Surah Maryam). That is, she wished she had died before standing in this distressing situation, although when the angel had earlier informed her that God would grant her a pure boy, she had marvelled, saying:

﴿How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?﴾ (Surah Maryam, 20).

That was merely wonder and calm emotion. But now that the matter has become actual birth, there must be an intense outburst expressing the bewilderment she is in, so she wished for death. Yet God, exalted is He, has forbidden us to wish for death, as came in the noble hadith that guides us, when life becomes narrow for us, not to wish for death, but to say: "O God, keep me alive as long as life is good for me, and cause me to die when death is good for me."

We have said that the forbidden wishing for death is that which involves objection to God's decree and rebellion against His will, such as hating life and living when it has become narrow for you so that you wish for death. But wishing for death because you know you will proceed to something better than what you leave behind is a different matter.

This question of wishing for death has appeared in the Qur'an in the discussion of the Children of Israel, who said: "We are the sons of God and His beloved," and said: "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days," and that the Last Abode is exclusively theirs with God. So how did the noble Qur'an respond to them?

Say: since the matter is as you claim, and the Hereafter is yours, ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 94).

Then the Truth, exalted is He, decreed what would happen from them, saying:

﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 95).

And He said of them: ﴿You will surely find them the most covetous of people for life﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 96).

Since they will not wish for death, and since they are the most covetous of people for life, their present life must be better in their estimation than the other life.

Therefore the believer may not wish for death to flee from a trial that has befallen him or in objection to God's decree, but he may do so if he knows that he is proceeding to something better than his present state. Her saying: ﴿a thing forgotten﴾ (Surah Maryam, 23).

The nasy is the trivial thing that is not regarded, and it is usually forgotten because of its unimportance, like a man who left behind with his friend a matchbox containing two matches, and on the way remembered it and returned to his friend asking for what he had forgotten. Thus Maryam wished to be a forgotten thing so that no one would remember her. She did not stop at this but said:

﴿a thing forgotten﴾ (Surah Maryam, 23), because the nasy is a trivial thing that is forgotten in its own right, but despite its triviality, perhaps someone will remember and recognise it, so she emphasised the nasy by her saying (mansiyyan), that is, that no one should remember it and no one should think of it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 24:

﴿Then he called her from beneath her: "Do not grieve..." 24﴾ (Surat Maryam).

In it there are two readings: (min) and (man). It is correct that Jibril (peace be upon him) was still present with her, but he was not beneath her, which shows that the one who called to her was the newborn child (al-Walid).

﴿Do not grieve...﴾ (Surat Maryam, 24).

Maryam's grief arose from her separation from people, from being in the state of giving birth with no one to support and assist her, and having no one with her to bring what this matter requires of food, drink and the like. Therefore her Lord, blessed and exalted, took care of her, and provided for her what would sustain her with food and drink. So He said:

﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾ (Surat Maryam, 24).

The sari (سري) is the river that flows with sweet, pure water, and then (He) gives her the food suited to her condition.

Thus the Exalted Lord provided Maryam with the essentials of life and the elements needed to sustain it, arranged according to their importance to a human being: air, drink, and food. A person can endure without food for a month, sustaining himself from the nourishment stored in his body, but he cannot endure without water for more than three to ten days, depending on the water content of his body. As for air, he cannot endure it for a single moment, and a person can die from holding his breath even once.

Therefore, it is from the wisdom of the Creator, glory be to Him, that He makes food plentiful, makes water scarce, and never gives anyone ownership of air. For if you were angry with someone and withheld air from him, he would die before you became pleased with him. So the elements of sustaining life are arranged according to their importance in human life, and the Exalted Lord guaranteed them for Maryam, placed them within her reach, and made her independent so that no one had to serve her.

Air was present while she was in the open desert; then water, for He made a sweet, clear stream flow beneath her; then food, and so He said:

﴿And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.﴾ [19:25]

It is as though the Blessed and Exalted Lord wished to show Maryam another of His signs. He commanded her to shake the trunk of the dry palm tree, which a strong man could not shake. How then, when she was weak, suffering the pains and hardships of childbirth?

Although the Exalted Lord is able to send down her food to her without any effort on her part and without her shaking anything, He willed to combine two things for her: seeking the means, and relying on the One who causes the means to act. Taking the means by shaking the palm tree, although she was exhausted, worn out by pregnancy and labor, and He brought her to the palm tree so she could lean on it and cling to it in her solitude, so that we would know that a human being in his striving is required to take the means, however weak he may be.

Therefore He left Maryam to take the means despite her weakness and inability, and then to rely on the Causer, glory be to Him, who sent down to her the dates, fully ripe and mature. And could Maryam have shaken this great, dry trunk?

It was merely a gesture indicating compliance with the command, while God Himself takes charge of sending down her food. The poet has depicted this situation in his words:

"Did you not see that God said to Maryam,
'Shake toward you the trunk, the ripe dates will fall,'
And if He willed, He would have given her without a shake,
But everything has a cause."

As for His words, ﴿it will drop upon you﴾, meaning: they will fall upon you. ﴿Ripe, fresh dates﴾, meaning: they have matured and become fit to be harvested, not picked prematurely before their time. Some dates fall before they ripen and are then not fit for eating.

His words ﴿it will drop upon you﴾ indicate the responsiveness and affectedness of inanimate things. Otherwise, the unripe date had not departed from the obedience of its mother; rather, it dropped willingly and in compliance when it had reached full ripeness.

And we notice here that when the Truth, blessed and exalted, provided sustenance for Maryam, He brought water first, saying:

﴿And your Lord has placed beneath you a stream.﴾ (Surah Maryam)

Then He brought food, saying:

﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.﴾ (Surah Maryam)

This is because water takes precedence over food in human need. But when giving the command to benefit from them, He said:

﴿So eat and drink..﴾ (Surah Maryam)

He began with food before drink. Why? Because a person usually eats first and then drinks. Water, despite its importance, customarily comes after food. Glory be to the One whose speech this is.

As for His saying:

﴿And let your eye be cooled..﴾ (Surah Maryam)

After the Truth, glorified is He, had supplied her with food and drink, which is the foundation of physical existence and by which life is sustained, a deep sorrow, pain, and bewilderment over her situation still remained within her. Therefore her Lord, blessed and exalted, after the sustenance that is the foundation of the body, gives her tranquility and calm, and relieves her of the pain of the soul and the bewilderment of the heart.

﴿And let your eye be cooled..﴾ (Surah Maryam): *qurri*, meaning "be at rest." In Arabic usage this expression is a kinayah (allusion) for joy. Among examples is the saying of Allah, the Exalted, on the tongue of Pharaoh's wife:

﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you..﴾ (Surah al-Qasas)

The Arabs express the coolness and stillness of the eye as joy, because the stillness of the eye on a single sight, not turning away from it, is evidence that the eye has encountered a beautiful sight in which a person finds happiness and delight, so that no other sight can replace it, and it remains still upon it without moving away.

This expression may also be used in the opposite sense, namely in evil and in invoking harm upon a person and wishing him ill. Such is the case of the woman who entered upon one of the caliphs, and he rebuked her. She said to him: "May God complete His blessing upon you and cool your eye." The attendees thought she was praying for him, but he perceived her intent and said to his companions: "Did you not understand what she said? She means, 'May God complete His blessing upon you,' that is, remove it. Have you not heard the poet's saying:

When a thing is complete, its decline appears;
Await its decline once it is said to be complete."

This is because a human being by nature is a child of change; he does not remain in one state. When he reaches the peak and blessing is complete for him, being a child of change, he must move away from it. Her saying "May God cool your eye" means: "May He blind you."

Thus the saying of Allah to Maryam:

﴿And let your eye be cooled..﴾ (Surah Maryam)

means: be happy with Allah's choosing you, and be pleased with what He has given you. What you worry about and grieve over is itself the blessing that no one other than you among the women of the worlds possesses. Then Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And if you see any human being, say, "Indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being."﴾ (Surah Maryam)

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted, takes up Maryam's defense and justifies her position, for which she herself finds no justification in people's customs. Who will seek an excuse for a woman who conceives and gives birth without having a husband? Whatever she says, she will not be believed, and she will not escape the tongues of the people and their disparagement.

So: the answer to what is disliked is silence. Therefore He commanded her to remain silent and not to dispute with anyone about her matter:

﴿So say, "Indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being."﴾ (Surah Maryam)

The fast here means abstention from speech, as happened in the story of Zakariya, because miracles are close to one another. Allah gave Zakariya [a sign] with the impairment of his faculties, and gave Maryam [a sign] with the deficiency of faculties. None justifies these miracles or defends them except their Maker, blessed and exalted.

Some who like to criticize the Qur'an raised an objection to this matter, saying: "How does He command her to fast from speech while at the same time commanding her to say, 'I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast'?"

It is possible that she said this phrase first, to the first human being she saw, so that her fast would be announced, and then she abstained from speech. It is also possible that what is meant by speech here is gesture. Indication by gestures is the strongest and most comprehensive form of indication. Although languages among humans differ, because each community agreed upon a particular language of its own, sign language remains a general language agreed upon by all. For example, when you nod your head like this, it means "yes" in all languages, and when you point with your finger like this, it means "no." So indication is a universal and general language. The Noble Qur'an touched on this matter elsewhere in His saying:

﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand any saying.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf)

That is, they were not near to comprehension; yet they understood by a fortiori reasoning, and nevertheless there was among them speech, gesture, and language, and each understood the other:

﴿They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog..."﴾ (Surah al-Kahf)

We notice in her saying:

﴿So I will not speak today to any human being.﴾ (Surah Maryam)

that the prohibition concerns speaking with humans specifically. She did not say, "I will not speak," for otherwise Jibril, peace be upon him, was with her speaking to her, and there was mutual understanding between them, perhaps he would see a way out for her. Maryam was confident and reassured about this way out. If her Lord, blessed and exalted, commanded her to fast from speech, then He would make the infant speak, so that he himself would speak and defend his mother against the accusations of the people.

When we discussed His saying:

﴿Then he called to her from beneath her, "Do not grieve.."﴾ (Surah Maryam)

we excluded that this call was from Jibril, and we said it was the call of the infant. Therefore Maryam was reassured and knew that she was before a great miracle, and she was entirely certain that when she pointed to him, he would speak himself and would remove the embarrassment from her with her people. This is because speech from one who is able to speak does not come with an argument that convinces people contrary to custom. But when he speaks while in the cradle, this means that he is a miracle that breaks habit. If the infant is a miracle, then the miracle in his mother is all the more so.

We marvel at Lady Mary. Instead of being ashamed of what had happened and hiding her child from people's eyes, or moving him to some other place in the wastes of the earth, she carried him, went with him, and brought him straight to her people. She would only have done this and dared to do it because of her confidence in the proof she had with her, which her child would vindicate for her.

Thus, when some Orientalists asked Imam Muhammad 'Abduh, may Allah have mercy on him, in Paris: "In what manner did 'A'isha face her people after the story of the slander?" Glory be to Allah, they know it is a slander and falsehood, yet they repeat it as if they do not understand.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, answered simply: "In the same manner that Mary faced her people while carrying her child." That is, with the bearing of one who is certain of innocence, confident in Allah's support, and certain that He, glorified is He, would never abandon her. Therefore, when the innocence of 'A'isha was revealed in the Book of Allah, they said to her: "Thank the Prophet." She said: "Rather, I thank Allah, who cleared me from above the seven heavens."

When the people saw her in this condition, they spoke harshly against her, saying:

﴿O Mary, you have certainly come with a thing unprecedented [fariyyan]﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:27).

Fariyyan (فرياً): al-Fary of the hide means cutting it up; and "amr fari" is a matter that is cut through in a way that is customary among people, so that there is nothing like it; or it derives from al-iftira', which is deliberately fabricating a lie.

Their words to Maryam:

﴿O sister of Harun...﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:28).

This is hurtful speech, a rebuke, and an exaggeration on their part in reproaching her. They attributed her to Harun, who was named after the Prophet (Harun, Aaron). It is as if they said: you come from a righteous household and were raised in obedience to God, so how could this deed come from you? Just as you would see a veiled woman who, in the street, does something that does not fit her appearance, and you blame her for this behaviour, which is not conceivable from one like her.

And His saying: ﴿Your father was not a man of evil...﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:28).

The "man of evil" (rajul su') is one whose companionship brings you evil, and who harms you with injury.

﴿...nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:28).

We have said: al-baghy (unchastity) is the woman who solicits men and invites them to herself. So the meaning is: from where did you get this trait, when you come from a good and righteous family?

In this is evidence that the influence of the family's upbringing affects the children. When we are a believing family and a home committed to the law of God, and when we embrace our children and surround them with care and nurture, we will receive a believing, conscious generation, beneficial to itself and to its society.

So their words:

﴿Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:28)

are a clear accusation against Maryam, and an affirmation that she had fallen into what is forbidden, as if they were insistent on hurling the charge of immorality at her.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 29:

Meaning: when the people said what they said, she (Maryam) pointed to the child (al-Walid), confident that he would speak, reassured that she was not carrying evidence of a crime but rather evidence of innocence. When she pointed to him, she said to her people: "Ask him." They were amazed:

﴿They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:29)

We note in their words that they did not find it unlikely that the child would speak. They did not say, "How can one who is in the cradle, a child, speak?" Rather they said: ﴿How can we speak..﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:29), meaning: we ourselves. So they found it unlikely that they would speak to him, as if they were disparaging themselves and their own ability to understand the child if he spoke to them.

Al-mahd (the cradle; literally, the prepared place): this is the place prepared and readied for a infant's sleep, because the infant cannot ward off harm from himself. An adult, for example, can prepare his own sleeping place, and remove from it whatever disturbs his sleep and comfort, and he has awareness, so if something pains him while sleeping he can shift out of the state he is in and look to see what is hurting him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 30:

It is as if he said to the people: "Do not speak, you; I am the one who will speak." Then he hastened to speak to them: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah..."﴾ (Surah Maryam, 30).

Thus Jesus, peace be upon him, began his speech by declaring his servanthood to Allah, the Exalted. In this is evidence that he might be claimed to be something other than a servant, that he is a god or a partner of God. Therefore, the first word he uttered was ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah..."﴾ (Surah Maryam, 30).

The miracle that came with me does not prevent my being a servant of Allah. Therefore, if you asked those who believe about Jesus, peace be upon him, that he is a god or a partner of God: "You say that he spoke in the cradle, so what did he say?" They will never acknowledge his words, because his statement and his utterance, ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 30), negate their belief from its foundation. And this is not all; rather: ﴿He has given me the Scripture...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 30).

But how did Allah give him the Scripture while he was still an infant in the cradle? They said: it is on the basis that it is a settled matter and an event without doubt, as if he is saying: "I am fit to bear the trust of heaven to the people of the earth." Although the Scripture had not yet come, it was already conferred on him by his Lord in fact, even though the time at which this Scripture would be delivered had not yet arrived.

﴿And has made me a prophet﴾ (Surah Maryam, 30).

My conduct is upright, and it cannot be open to reproach after this. And if there is any reproach, it is far from me, and I am not to blame for it.

Meaning: "and He has also enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I remain alive." Isa (peace be upon him) spoke these words in the cradle to clear his blessed mother, the truthful one (al-Siddiqah), for they had accused her of the thing most precious to her; therefore no words from her would have benefited, and to rescue her, the truth was conveyed to her through Jibril or through Isa (peace be upon them both) that she should say:

﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being.﴾ (Surah Maryam)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 32:

Why does he mention his mother here, and why is he so keen to affirm his kindness toward her? They say: because some may think that Jesus, peace be upon him, when he grows up and learns the story of his birth, that his mother brought him without a father, untouched by any human, may have this matter leave shadows in his soul, and doubts may stir within him about his mother. So he wanted to cut off all these suspicions.

That is because he himself is the proof, and he himself is the witness to his mother's innocence, and a proof does not cast doubt on what it proves. It is as if he is saying to the people: beware of thinking that I would dare to act arrogantly toward my mother, or that any evil thought toward her would occur to me. Then he says:

﴿And [He has made me dutiful to my mother] and has not made me a tyrant, disobedient.﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:32)

He thereby negated from himself the attribute of tyranny, harshness and arrogance, because the messenger must be gentle in manner and kind toward his people, since he came to bring people out of the corruption they were accustomed to into obedience that weighs heavily upon them.

A human being, by nature, when he has become accustomed to corruption, dislikes the one who takes him out of his corruption. So it is natural that the Prophet should be subjected to the provocation, obstinacy and arrogance of his people. Had he not been gentle in manner, soft in speech, winning over the ears so that they listen and the hearts so that they understand, he would not have been fit for this mission. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, addresses His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, saying:

﴿And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you...﴾ (Surah Ali 'Imran 3:159)

The meaning of ﴿shaqiyyan﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:32) is: disobedient, and how far is one whose attributes are these from the disobedience of God, through which a person becomes wretched.

Earlier we said, in the story of Yahya (peace be upon him), that these events are three signposts in a person's life: the day of his birth, the day of his death, and the day he is raised up on the Day of Resurrection. So what is the aspect of safety (salam) in these events with respect to 'Isa (peace be upon him)?

His saying: ﴿And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾ [19:33].

As for the day of his birth, it passed in peace despite the wonders that accompanied it. No one harmed him, though he was a child who came without a father, and some zealous, jealous people could have attacked him and his mother with harm. But nothing of that happened, and his birth passed in peace for him and for his mother.

﴿And the day I die﴾ [19:33]: they took him to crucify him, but God saved him from their hands, cast his likeness upon another person, and raised him to heaven.

﴿And the day I am raised alive﴾ [19:33]: there is no messenger among the messengers who will be questioned in this way and debated in this manner, the debate which 'Isa was subjected to in this world:

﴿And when God says, "O 'Isa son of Maryam, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" He will say, "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not say to them except what You commanded me: 'Worship God, my Lord and your Lord.'"﴾ [5:116–117].

This is not a disparagement of the station of 'Isa (peace be upon him), for his Lord, blessed and exalted, knows that he did not say to his people except what he was commanded. Rather, God intended to rebuke the people who took him and his mother as two gods besides God. Thus the aspect of peace in the day

﴿I am raised alive﴾ [19:33] is that he was questioned in this world and his innocence was established.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 34:

﴿That is﴾ (Surah Maryam), i.e., what has preceded of the story of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him). ﴿the word of truth﴾ (Surah Maryam), i.e., God Most High says it as a word of truth. The Truth (al-Ḥaqq) is God, so the One who related to you this account is God, and His word is the truth in which there is no falsehood. Thus "truth" here is the opposite of falsehood (bāṭil), and the two meanings converge. Or: the intended "word of truth" is the word "Be" (kun), by which creation is completed.

Then God Most High says:

﴿about which they dispute﴾ (Surah Maryam).

From al-mirāʾ (mirā'): it means disagreement and argument in falsehood. The Truth, glorified is He, knows that they will doubt it and argue about it in falsehood, and that they will spread various sayings concerning it. It is as if God Most High is saying to them: Leave these sayings and falsehoods concerning the matter of ʿĪsā, and take what I have informed you of his account, for it is the truth, to which falsehood does not come from before it or from behind it.

Why did the Almighty specifically mention the negation of offspring here?

They said: Because the matter of a partner for God is negated by primary reason. If every god were capable of both acting and refraining, this would be a repeated form that does not befit a god. And if this one is a god for such-and-such and that one is a god for such-and-such, then neither has a deficiency compared to the other, and this is impossible for a god. Moreover, if there were another god, each of them would have gone off with a part, as He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Otherwise each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others.﴾ (Surat al-Mu'minun: 91)

Therefore He negated the matter of offspring, because it has a special importance with regard to the story of Jesus, peace be upon him; for offspring may be the subject of a false inference, because its proof is the taking of a child or the love of a child, and a person loves a child and strives toward him. Why?

They said: Because a person is a son of his worldly life, and he knows that he is dying, dying, so he loves to have an extension in the world and a remembrance after him. A person clings to the world even after his death, and he does not realize that a man's remembrance does not come after him; rather, his remembrance precedes him to the Hereafter through righteous deeds.

So, love of offspring here is for the perpetuation of preserving life, and this is impossible with regard to Allah, blessed and exalted is He, because He is the Everlasting who does not cease.

Offspring may also be taken to be a support for one's father, a backer and helper, and this is a sign of weakness, while the Almighty is the Strong who does not need anyone's help. So taking offspring is something negated of Him, blessed and exalted is He; it is a matter that does not befit the station of divinity, and you must declare God far above having offspring. Therefore, after this He says:

﴿Glory be to Him.﴾ (Surat Maryam: 35)

The word "Subhan" (Glory; the term denoting absolute transcendence) indicates the absolute declaration of God's transcendence, in His essence, His attributes, and His acts. He, glorified is He, is "not like unto Him is anything" (Surat al-Shura: 11). Even if a shared attribute is found between you and God, such as that God has a face and a hand and you have a face and a hand, beware of descending to the highest level and saying: "His face is like my face," or "His hand is like my hand," for you have existence and God has existence. Is your existence like God's existence?

Your existence was preceded by non-existence and will be followed by non-existence, whereas His existence, exalted is He, was not preceded by non-existence and will not be followed by non-existence. So you must say in such matters:

﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (Surat al-Shura: 11)

Whoever traces the root (س ب ح) in the Noble Qur'an finds that it came in all forms:

The past tense: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God.﴾ (Surat al-Hadid: 1)

The present tense: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God.﴾ (Surat al-Jumu'ah: 1)

And the imperative: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.﴾ (Surat al-A'la: 1)

Since the whole universe glorifies God and has not ceased its glorification, but is still glorifying, when He created creation He commanded them to glorify, because they are part of the glorifying system of the universe, and they must align with it and not be a discord in God's universe.

As for the verbal noun (subhan), it came to indicate the absolute transcendence of God, even before He created creation, and transcendence is established for Him before He created anyone to declare Him transcendent, as in His saying:

﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed.﴾ (Surat al-Isra': 1)

because the matter is wondrous and beyond the grasp of reason. He brought the verbal noun (subhan), which indicates the absolute transcendence of God, as if He, exalted is He, warns those who rule by their intellects and do not submit God's power, who created them, to the laws of time, place, distance and space. For every act is proportionate in strength and capacity to its doer.

Then He, exalted is He, says:

﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (Surat Maryam: 35)

That is because the verse concerning the creation of Jesus, peace be upon him, contradicts all the laws and breaks the habit people are accustomed to. So beware of marveling at God's act concerning Yahya, for He brought him when the instruments were worn out, or marveling at the creation of Jesus, for He brought him with a lack of instruments.

And beware of marveling at the speech of Jesus while he was an infant in the cradle, for these are indeed matters that break the habit and the laws. So take them within the frame of (Glory be to Him) and declare Him transcendent, for when He wills something He does not treat it by work and effort, but rather He treats it with (Be), and it is.

And do not suppose that the creation of things depends on this command (Be). If the verb is composed of (kaf) and (nun), then before the nun is pronounced the thing already exists. But (Be) is the shortest that can be conceived by us, and the Almighty addresses us with what brings this matter closer to our minds; otherwise His will, glorified is He, has no need of the word (Be), for what God wills occurs merely by His will. Also, if you look closely at His saying:

﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (Surat Maryam: 35)

you find (He says to it), i.e., to the thing, as if the thing already exists in actuality, existing eternally. So the command "Be" is not for bringing it into existence from nothing, but merely for manifesting it in the realm of reality.

Al-Rabb: He is the One who takes charge of nurturing and caring (for His creation). Tarbiyah (upbringing, nurturing) means that the one who nurtures (al-murabbi) guides the one being nurtured (al-murabba) through training to that which will make him fit to carry out his task and perform it. For example, if you want an engineer, you raise him in the manner of an engineer; and if you want a physician, you raise him in the manner of a physician. Here we are faced with a people who have associated partners with God, and we need a caller (da'iyah) who will bring them out of shirk (associating partners with God) to faith (iman), and out of disobedience (ma'siyah) to obedience (ta'ah).

So the meaning is: since God, exalted is He, is my Lord and your Lord, and the One who takes charge of nurturing us all, then He must nurture for you someone who will set you right, because He, exalted is He, does not address you directly. Rather, He will send me to you to convey His message to you, and I call you to worship Him alone, without partner. And since God is my Lord and your Lord, it is obligatory upon you to obey Him: ﴿So worship Him...﴾ [Surah Maryam 19:36].

Worship (ibadah) is that the worshipper obeys the one he worships in His commands and His prohibitions, as God, exalted is He, said:

﴿And they were not commanded except to worship God, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining toward prayer and giving zakah. And that is the correct religion.﴾ [Surah al-Bayyinah 98:5]

Then God, exalted is He, says:

﴿This is a straight path﴾ [Surah Maryam 19:36], meaning: one in which there is no crookedness and no deviation, and it is the way that brings you to your goal by the shortest route and with the least effort. It is well known that a straight line is the shortest distance between two points.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 19, verse 37:

Al-Ahzab (the factions): those among his people who differed about Jesus (peace be upon him). Some of them said he is God, some said he is the son of God, and another said he is the third of three. Some of them accused him of sorcery, and some of them said of him: "He is the son of adultery." We seek God's forgiveness for what the wrongdoers and the disbelievers say.

Al-Ahzab is the plural of hizb, and they are a group of people who gather around a principle or an opinion among opinions, defending it and believing in it, living their lives according to it, and subordinating the movement of their lives to serving it.

As for the meaning of His words, ﴿from among them﴾ (Surat Maryam, 37):

That is, from within those who believed in him and from among Jesus's own followers. Those who said these falsehoods about him were not his enemies but were among those who believed in him. Thus the people differed concerning the matter of Jesus, and each of them had an opinion, and all of them were contrary to the truth and far from reality. Therefore the Creator, glorified is He, threatened them with His saying:

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, because of the scene of a great Day﴾ (Surat Maryam, 37)

You said about Jesus what you said in this world, and you plunged into him with whatever speech you wished, because God, exalted is He, made your will effective over your limbs and gave you freedom of action and choice. So you directed your limbs and chose what angers God. It is as though the punishment of this world does not match what they did, and there must be for them a deferred punishment in the Hereafter that matches what occurred from them against their Prophet and against their Lord, blessed and exalted is He.

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, because of the scene of a great Day﴾ (Surat Maryam, 37)

The scene of a great Day is the Day of Resurrection, the Day when hidden things are laid bare, the Day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds, the Day when no soul will have power to avail another soul in anything, and the command that Day belongs to God.

He called it "the great scene" because it is a witnessed day that everyone witnesses. The punishment of this world, for example, is witnessed only by those present in its time, and it is not witnessed by those who came before or those who come after. But the punishment of the Hereafter is the great scene that all creation sees.

Perhaps some punishment is easier than another's seeing a person while he is being punished, for a person may bear the punishment within himself, but that he is punished in the sight of all people, and they see him in this humiliation and this abasement, when in this world he was great, or a tyrant, or an oppressor, there is no doubt that their seeing him in this state is more painful and more effective against him.

Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says about them in another verse:

﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and say, "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers"﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 27)

This from them is merely words:

﴿But there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 28). That is, what they used to conceal has become apparent to them, and He did not say "has been concealed from them," as though they had known something about it but had hidden it. And He said about them:

﴿And if you could see when the criminals will bow their heads before their Lord, saying, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are now certain"﴾ (Surat as-Sajdah, 12).

Why have they now seen and heard? Because in the world they used to hear without awareness, so they denied, and they saw the signs of God in the universe and did not believe. But in the Hereafter the realities that they had long denied have been uncovered to them, and there is no longer any room for obstinacy or denial.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 38:

His saying:

﴿How well they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:38). That is: how well they will hear, and how well they will see. This is one of the forms of exclamation on the pattern of "af'al bihi" (how [verb] he is), meaning: how keen their hearing is, and how keen their sight is. They now sharpen their hearing and scrutinise their sight, so much so that a person marvels at their precise hearing and all-encompassing sight, after they had been in the world putting their fingers in their ears so they would not hear, and covering their garments over themselves so they would not see. They were blind to the clear signs of God that establish the truthfulness of the messengers, to the verses that carry the legal rulings, and to the cosmic signs that point to the power of the Wise Creator.

And His saying: ﴿on the Day they come to Us﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:38). That is: how well they will hear and how well they will see on this Day, the Day of Resurrection. Man, by virtue of God Most High having created him and made him vicegerent on earth, has been given mastery over his limbs; he commands them and they obey him. The limbs of man and his capacities are subjected to his will. Your tongue can utter "There is no god but God," and it can equally say "There is no god," or say "God is the third of three." The tongue is compliant with you; it does not disobey you in this or that. God gave you this freedom and guaranteed you this choice only because He will hold you to account for it on the Day of Resurrection: "Did you want the good to which He directed you, or did you want the evil from which He forbade you?"

As for the Day of Resurrection, this will is dissolved and its authority over the limbs is annulled, on a Day when the Truth, blessed and exalted, calls out:

﴿Whose is the sovereignty today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (Surah Ghafir, 40:16). On that Day the limbs will testify against their owner, as the Truth, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 24:24).

And He, exalted, says:

﴿They will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "God has made us speak, who makes everything speak."﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 41:21).

Why not? Since the limbs have been freed from the bondage of the will, the time has come for them to complain to God and to utter the word of truth that they had concealed under the pressure and coercion of the will.

We have previously given an example of this: a group of soldiers marching under the direct command of their immediate officer, obeying his orders with blind obedience. But when they return to the supreme commander, their tongues break out in complaint about the tyranny and arrogance of their immediate officer.

Then He, exalted, says:

﴿But the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:38).

Would that they had understood this matter! But they did wrong, and they wronged only themselves. God, blessed and exalted, is not harmed by the disbelief of the disbelievers, nor does it diminish His kingdom and sovereignty, exalted is He. But how does a person wrong himself?

A person wrongs himself because he possesses a conscious mind that receives things and distinguishes them, and he possesses a appetitive soul which, with its immediate desires, collides with this conscious mind and collides with the divine method that commands it to good and forbids it from evil. This soul, with its appetites, calls the person toward its aims and casts him into momentary pleasure and transient delight, which entail punishment and cause him to forfeit lasting good and everlasting bliss.

Therefore He, exalted, says:

﴿But people wrong themselves.﴾ (Surah Yunus, 10:44).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 39:

Allah the Exalted says:

﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe.﴾ (Surah Maryam: 39)

Al-inḏār (warning) is alerting someone to an evil that is coming. Al-ḥasrah (regret) is the intense remorse that afflicts the human soul when it loses a good that cannot be made up, or when it faces something it cannot repel. Regret about a good that has been missed but can still be made up is only sorrow. For example, a student who fails an exam in one month regrets it, but he can make up for this failure the following month. If he fails the final exam of the year, however, he feels severe remorse and grieves over a year that has passed, whose loss cannot be recovered.

Therefore, on the Day of Resurrection the disbelievers will say:

﴿Alas for us, for what we neglected concerning it.﴾ (Surah al-An'am: 31)

The meaning is: "Alas for us! This is your time, O regret, so come forth, for the opportunity has passed never to return." So the Day of Regret is the Day of Resurrection, when no one can return to make up for the good he missed in the world. Would that minds understood this truth and acted upon it while they still have room in the world.

As for the phrase:

﴿When the matter has been decided﴾ (Surah Maryam: 39), it means: it has occurred and taken place, and it cannot be averted, and there is no longer any room to make up for what has been missed. This is because the One who decided this matter and judged it is Allah, blessed and exalted, whom no one can reject His command, postpone it from its appointed time, or dispute with Him about it. Glory be to Him; the command is His command, the decree is His decree, and there is no god but Him.

It is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "When Allah admits the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of Hellfire into Hellfire, He will bring Death in the form of a ram. He will say to the believers: 'Do you recognise this?' They will say: 'Yes, it is Death, which came to us, and we recognised it.' He will say to the disbelievers: 'Do you recognise this?' They will say: 'We recognise it.' Then Allah will slaughter Death, and He will say to the people of Paradise: 'Eternity without death.' And to the people of the Fire: 'Eternity without death.'"

Thus Allah decided the matter in order to cut off hope from the disbelievers, who might think that Death would come to release them from the torment they are in and bring them rest. Allah cut off this hope and despaired them of it, by bringing Death in visible form and slaughtering it before them. There is no death after this, for Death has died. Concerning them the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf: 77)

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿while they are in heedlessness and do not believe﴾ (Surah Maryam: 39).

Heedlessness (al-ghaflah) is when a person turns his mind away from reflecting on something whose proof of its soundness is clear, because Allah, blessed and exalted, would not punish His creation unless He had made clear to them the evidences that a sound intellect receives and believes in.

So whoever does not believe is either heedless of these proofs, or wilfully neglectful of them, or denies them, as He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance.﴾ (Surah al-Naml: 14)

Among heedlessness is their heedlessness of death. They said: "Whoever dies, his Resurrection has come." Among the wisdom of Allah is that He made death indefinite: indefinite in time, indefinite in cause, and indefinite in place. Thus the indefiniteness of death is itself its clarification, because its indefiniteness makes a person ready to meet it at any time, by any cause, and in any place. Death comes unexpectedly, since it is not bound to a particular time, cause or place.

A child dies while still in his mother's womb, or dies a day or days after his birth, or dies after a hundred years. He dies by a cause and without a cause. We may marvel at one of us dying suddenly with no apparent cause: a car did not strike him, a wall or a stone did not fall on him, and no illness overtook him. What is the cause? The cause is death. He will die, that is, he died because he is mortal, as it is said: "Death without causes is the cause."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 19, verse 40:

How can the Truth, glory be to Him, say:

﴿We shall inherit the earth and whatever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:40)

Yet the earth and the whole universe belong to Him, exalted is He? They said: Because He, blessed and exalted, is the Supreme Owner, and He has given some of His creation ownership. This is in the world. As for the Hereafter, no one has ownership over anything. A person has no control even over his own limbs and members. So the command on that Day belongs entirely to God, exalted is He, and ownership returns to its Supreme Owner, and no one inherits this ownership except God, exalted is He.

Therefore, those who were deceived by God's blessings in this world and thought they would have the like of them in the Hereafter, one of them said:

﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 18:36)

We say to him: No. It is true that you will be returned to your Lord, but you will have nothing with Him, because the One who made you a owner in this world made you owner from within His own ownership, exalted is He. So when the Hereafter comes, He alone is the Inheritor.

As for His saying: ﴿And to Us they will be returned.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:40), it means: the matter does not stop at our inheriting their possessions while they go on their way. Rather, We shall inherit their ownership and then they will return to Us so that We may call them to account, and they too will not escape the grip of ownership.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 41:

After the Almighty spoke, at the opening of Surah Maryam, of the birth of our master Yahya to Zakariya, and of the birth of our master al-Masih from Maryam, He wished to set before us a procession of the messages He sent down as a light from heaven to guide the earth, so He said:

﴿And mention in the Book Ibrahim.. " 41 "﴾ (Surah Maryam)

For he is the father of the prophets and their pinnacle, because Allah the Exalted praised him when He said:

﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation.. " 120 "﴾ (Surah an-Nahl).

There is no single individual who contains all the qualities of perfection and all the gifts of excellence. Rather, the whole contains them. This one is brave and strong of build, this one is intelligent, this one has keen sight, this one excels in medicine, and this one in agriculture. Gifts are scattered among mankind, and none of them gathers them: neither his strength, nor his life, nor his effort can make him gifted in everything. Thus perfection as a whole is distributed among creation, except Ibrahim, peace be upon him, who in his gifts equalled an entire nation.

As for His saying:
﴿Indeed, he was a truthful one (siddiq), a prophet.. " 41 "﴾ (Surah Maryam)

Siddiq: from the root ṣ-d-q, and its meaning is to speak in accordance with reality, since lying is to speak contrary to reality. This is called "truthful in himself" (ṣādiq). As for our saying "siddiq", it means an intensification of truthfulness: he has reached the utmost in affirming what comes from the Almighty, the Blessed and Exalted. He obeys and submits without debate, as we saw of the mother of Musa, peace be upon him, when the Almighty said to her:
﴿And when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve.. " 7 "﴾ (Surah al-Qasas)

By God, could a mother accept this speech and comply with this command? How could she save her child from an assumed harm or death by a certain death?

Therefore, this is a speech that is not credible and lies beyond the reach of reason for ordinary people. But in the procession of messages the matter is different. When Musa's mother heard this call, no thought contrary to God's command crossed her mind, and no doubt about it besieged her, because the inspiration of God among these people is never opposed by the inspiration of Satan, and this is an established matter for the messengers.

Therefore, the siddiq is one who has reached the utmost in affirming the truth, so God bestows upon him transparency and illumination, such that he is guided to the truth and distinguishes it from falsehood at the first glance, without searching and scrutiny of the matter, because God the Exalted gives you the light that dispels the clouds of doubt from you, and gives you the precise balance by which you weigh things, as He the Glorified said:

﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion.. " 29 "﴾ (Surah al-Anfal).

And Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was named siddiq not because he is truthful in himself, but because he affirms everything that came to him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore, when they informed him of the news of the Night Journey and Ascension, which many denied, what did he say?

He said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth."

So the matter for him rested on the mere words of the Messenger of Allah. This was his standard, and as long as the Messenger of Allah had said it, it was true, without argument, without dispute, and without investigation into the circumstances of this matter. Therefore, from that day he has been siddiq by merit. And regarding Lady Maryam, the Almighty, the Blessed and Exalted said:

﴿And his mother was a truthful woman (siddiqah).. " 75 "﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah).

He named her siddiqah because she affirmed when the angel said to her:
﴿He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to grant you a pure boy.. " 19 "﴾ (Surah Maryam).

So she trusted this good news and took it as an established reality. When the boy came, she pointed to him while in complete confidence and full certainty that he would speak and talk.

Therefore, the siddiq is not one who affirms, but one who is affirmed (i.e., who is made to affirm by the truth). Thus Ibrahim, the Friend of Allah, was a siddiq and was also a nabi (prophet), because a person may be a siddiq, to whom God gives a special transparency, and it is not necessary that he be a prophet, just as Maryam was siddiqah and Abu Bakr was siddiq. This, then, is an innate, illuminating quality from God. As for prophethood, it is a gift and legislation that comes from above, and a guidance that descends from heaven, bearing the prophet his responsibility.

This is the discourse of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to his father, on the basis that he was a prophet who came to correct people's conduct according to the method of Allah, and the first of them was his father. The Qur'an has mentioned him in this way, by his fatherhood of Ibrahim, without mentioning his name, except in one verse in which it says:

﴿To his father, Azar...﴾ (Surat al-An'am) [74]

This verse has raised a problem, and some have thought that Azar was the real biological father of Ibrahim.

This view contradicts the noble Prophetic hadith that clarifies the purity of the origin of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), where he said: "I am the best of the best. I have continually passed from the loins of pure men to the wombs of pure women."

Thus, the ancestors of the Prophet up to Adam were "a pure man married to a pure woman." So if we said that Azar, of whom Allah said:

﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him...﴾ (Surat al-Tawba) [114]

was the father of Ibrahim, that would contradict the Prophetic hadith. How could there be among the forefathers of Muhammad (ﷺ) such an unbeliever?

If we reflect on the usages of fatherhood in the Noble Qur'an, we will be freed from this problem. The Qur'an speaks of direct biological fatherhood, and it speaks of indirect fatherhood in the case of the grandfather and in the case of the paternal uncle. It calls the grandfather a father, and the uncle a father, because he shares with my father a common grandfather, so he has an intermediary through which he deserved to be called a father. In the Qur'an there are two texts: one applies the term father to the grandfather, and the other applies it to the uncle.

The first is in the words of Allah the Exalted, from the story of Yusuf (peace be upon him):

﴿And there entered with him into prison two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine," and the other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread on my head, of which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good."﴾ (Surat Yusuf) [36]

They chose Yusuf to interpret their dreams because they saw him as one of the doers of good. It is as if goodness has known measures even among those who are not themselves good. When they faced a matter that concerned them, they resorted only to this good man. Thus the standards of perfection are respected and regarded even by one who lacks perfection.

When they said to him: ﴿Indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good﴾ [36],

he knew that they were following his movements and conduct, and how he behaved among them. So he wished to increase them from what he had of illuminations. His matter was not merely good conduct and a fine manner among them; rather, he had other things. So he said:

﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you...﴾ [37] (Surat Yusuf)

Then he left answering their question and began speaking about what concerned him as a prophet and a caller to Allah. He informed them that what he had of gifts was a gift from Allah, and that he was not cleverer than them. He said:

﴿That is of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and who, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers. And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Ibrahim and Ishaq and Ya'qub...﴾ [37-38] (Surat Yusuf)

Then he draws the attention of his companions to the falsehood of what they were upon, worshipping scattered lords who did not benefit them in anything. Behold, they leave them and resort to Yusuf, who has one Lord:

﴿O two companions of the prison, are scattered lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [39] (Surat Yusuf)

Thus Yusuf the prophet and caller was eager to spread his call and guide those around him. Even while in his prison he did not forget his mission, nor did he fall short in his call. When he finished his admonition and was able, with tact, to make them hear what he wanted, (he would not have succeeded) had he answered their question from the outset, for they would have turned away from this admonition and not paid it any attention.

Now he returns to their question and the interpretation of their dreams:

﴿As for one of you, he will give wine to his lord to drink; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.﴾ [41] (Surat Yusuf)

The evidence in this story is His saying:

﴿And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Ibrahim and Ishaq and Ya'qub...﴾ [38] (Surat Yusuf)

Yusuf is the son of Ya'qub, son of Ishaq, son of Ibrahim, so he called the grandfathers "fathers." And he may call the uncle a father, as came in His saying:

﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and we are Muslims [submitting] to Him."﴾ [133] (Surat al-Baqara)

So Isma'il is counted among the fathers of Ya'qub, though he was his uncle.

Therefore: if the Noble Qur'an, when speaking of the father of Ibrahim, had said "to his father" in every verse, the meaning would have gone to literal biological fatherhood. But that it says, even once: ﴿To his father, Azar...﴾ [74] (Surat al-An'am), this means that what is intended is his uncle, because the word "father" after fatherhood is not used except when we want the uncle, as we say now when we want the real father: "Your father came," without naming him, whereas for non-literal fatherhood we say: "Your father so-and-so came."

Accordingly, His saying ﴿To his father, Azar...﴾ [74] (Surat al-An'am) came only once, to establish for us that Azar was not the biological father of Ibrahim, but rather his uncle; and thereby the purity of the lineage of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the cleanness of his chain back to Adam (peace be upon him) is preserved. As for His saying ﴿O father...﴾ [42] (Surat Maryam), the Arabic construction would require him to say "ya abi" (O my father), but they drop the ya of the first person and compensate for it with a taa', so why? They said: because "abat" has a subtle nuance: he wishes to establish that, although he is a father, there is in him the tenderness of both parents, the father and the mother. So he used the taa', which points to the other side. For this reason it is said only in absolute tenderness, "ya abat," as if the mother had died, for example, so the father takes on both roles together and makes up to the children for the lost mother's tenderness.

As for His saying ﴿Why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and does not avail you at all?﴾ [42] (Surat Maryam):

From the manner of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) with his father appears the etiquette of da'wa, as he presented the admonition in the form of a question, so that his father would not feel inferior, or appear to him as though he knew more than him.

﴿Why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and does not avail you at all?﴾ [42]

We note that he did not say at the beginning, "Why do you worship Satan?" Rather, he delayed this truth until the end of the discussion. Instead of saying "Satan," he analysed his character, clarified his elements, and uncovered his reality: he does not hear, does not see, and does not avail you at all. These attributes do not belong to the one worshipped, and they are the reason we avoid worshipping anything besides Allah, whether a tree, a stone, or a devil, especially in the environment of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), which was full of idols and images.

For what does worship mean? It means the obedience of the worshipper to the worshipped in its commands and prohibitions. Those who worship other than Allah, whether an idol, a statue, the sun or the moon: what have these objects commanded them? From what have they forbidden them? What have these objects prepared for those who worship them? And what have they prepared for those who disobey them? What method did they bring that would make them deserving of worship? None of this exists. Therefore, their worship is false.

Abraham, the Prophet of Allah, repeats this tender call once more, as if he wishes to stir his father's sense of compassion and awaken the bonds of kinship in him. It is as if he is saying to him: my speech to you is the speech of a son to his father, just as we do today when one of us wishes to soften his father's heart; he says, "O my father, such-and-such... O my father, listen to me." This was Abraham's way, peace be upon him, for he called his father with this address four times in succession in these verses, and this was only out of his eagerness for his guidance and his taking him by the hand to the straight path.

And his saying:

﴿O my father, there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you...﴾ [19:43]: That is, do not think, O my father, that I consider myself superior to you, or that I am more excellent than you, or more intelligent than you. This speech is not from me, but from One who is higher than me and higher than you. So there is no shame in hearing it and submitting to it. It is a message I have been commissioned to convey to you. And this knowledge that has come to me has not come to you. This is a gentle apology from the Friend of Allah (khalil Allah). The matter is not a personal one between a son and his paternal uncle, or a son and his father; it is a general matter that transcends the bounds of fatherhood and paternal kinship.

For this reason, when we spoke in Surah al-Kahf about the story of Musa and al-Khidr, peace be upon them both, we said that the righteous servant made excuses for Musa, because he acted on the basis of knowledge that he had and that Musa did not have like it. So he said to him:

﴿And how can you have patience concerning that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ [18:68]. Likewise, Abraham said to his father so that pride would not seize him and he would not disdain listening to his son. Then he says:

﴿So follow me; I will guide you to a straight path.﴾ [19:43]: Because this method to which I invite you is not from me, but from One who is higher than me and higher than you. And al-Sirat al-sawi (the straight path) is the road that brings you to the goal with the least hardship and in the shortest time.

We note that Ibrahim, at the start of his address to his father, said:

﴿O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees, nor avails you anything...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:42).

Yet Satan can hear and see, so how is this to be understood?

They said: Because it is Satan who beautifies the worship of an idol, a tree, the sun or the moon, so the matter is traced back to him and he is its cause. However, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) addressed the matter directly, because his father worshipped an idol that neither hears nor sees and avails him nothing, and this is by their own testimony, as stated in His words, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿Do they hear you when you call? Or do they benefit you or harm you?﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara, 26:72-73).

This is a question, and a disputant who puts a question to his opponent about something never asks unless he knows that the answer must be in his favour, since he has entrusted him with the answer. Therefore, the worship of what is other than God traces back to the seduction of Satan.

Then Ibrahim continues, saying:

﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been to the Most Merciful a disobedient one.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:44).

"ASiyyan" (عصياً, disobedient): an intensive form of disobedience (ʿiṣyān). Satan is not merely disobedient; rather, he is excessively disobedient, defying the commands of God with obstinacy and stubbornness.

Al-Sha'rawi's Tafsir (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 19, verse 45:

The Friend of Allah (Khalil Allah) continued to be gentle in calling his father, so he said:

﴿O my father, I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so that you become a companion of Satan.﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:45)

He did not say "will befall you" (yusibaka). He did not want to shock him with this reality. The word "massa" (touch) means a light contact, as if he were saying: "Your affair concerns me, and I fear for you that even the mere dust of it may reach you." This is the utmost of compassion for him and of eagerness for his salvation.

Then he says: ﴿So you would become a companion of Satan﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:45). That is, close to him and following him, so that you would suffer the punishment that befalls him, and be tormented as he is tormented.

Thus ended this dialogue, which contained four tender calls, and it came as a unique model of calling to Allah with wisdom and good admonition. It respected the feelings of a father whose son calls him and offers him advice, arranged matters in a natural order, and linked them in a gentle sequence that neither provokes the listener's anger nor shocks him.

Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, has also taken account of the aspects of the human soul, and commanded that the call to Him be made with wisdom and good admonition, so that the one called is not burdened with both the harshness of the call and the harshness of having to abandon what he is accustomed to and move to what he is not accustomed to.

When you call a person to Allah, you are in fact taking him out of the corruption he has become used to. He did not become accustomed to corruption except after first desiring it, and then becoming habituated to it through action and practice. These are two calamities gripping his reins, so how much he needs a gentle method that wins his feelings and inclines him toward you, so that he responds to you.

The caller in this situation is like one who carefully works to extract silk from among thorns. If you scold him and are harsh with him, he will turn away from you, withdraw from your call, and remain in the corruption he is in. For this reason the Exalted said:

﴿Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition, and argue with them in the way that is best.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:125)

And they say: "Advice is heavy, so do not send it as a mountain, and do not make it a dispute." And they said: "Truths are bitter, so borrow for them the lightness of eloquence."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 19, verse 46:

The verb raghiba (رغب) carries both a meaning and its opposite, depending on the preposition that follows it. We say: raghiba fi kadha, meaning he loved it and went towards it; and raghiba 'an kadha, meaning he disliked it and withdrew from it. So the meaning of ﴿Do you turn away from my gods, Abraham?﴾ (Surah Maryam) is: you are abandoning them for something else. Likewise, in the words of the Most High:

﴿And who would turn away from the creed of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 130): that is, who leaves it for another creed.

We note that the verb raghiba was never followed by a negation except once, although fi (في) is implied after the verb. This is in the Most High's words concerning marrying orphan women: ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 127).

Desire for a thing means loving it and longing for it, and desire for a thing also means the path that leads to it. However, you have not actually taken this path, and you have not adopted the means that would lead you to what you desire. This meaning is clear in the story of the people of the garden in Surah (Nun), where the Most High says:

﴿We have tested them as We tested the owners of the garden, when they swore that they would harvest its fruit in the morning, without making any exception. Then a visitation from your Lord swept over it while they were asleep, and it became like the cut-down harvest.﴾ (Surah al-Qalam, 17–20)

They agreed to pick the fruit of their orchard in the morning and did not say, "If God wills." So God destroyed it and annihilated it while they slept. In the morning they set out to their garden, saying among themselves:

﴿No needy person shall enter it today against you﴾ (Surah al-Qalam, 24). Thus they cut off the path for themselves when they deprived the needy. ﴿When they saw it, they said, "We have surely gone astray. Rather, we are deprived."﴾ (Surah al-Qalam, 26–27). Then they became aware of the error they had fallen into, returned to their right course, and said:

﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we are turning towards our Lord.﴾ (Surah al-Qalam, 32): that is, we are desiring the path that leads to Him, the Most High. So before you say, "I desire God," the matter is not love alone, but love at a price, with striving and action that bring you to what you love. Therefore: before you can be desirous of your Lord, turn yourselves towards Him first.

In another place the Most High says: ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the alms﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 58): that is, they criticize you in their distribution of it.

﴿If they are given from it, they are pleased; but if they are not given from it, behold, they become resentful.﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 58)

They therefore do not love God; rather they love giving and fleeting worldly goods. This is shown by the fact that when they were denied, they became angry and turned their attention away from the religion of God, like those about whom God said:

﴿And among the people is he who worships God on an edge: if good befalls him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 11)

Therefore the Most High corrects their conduct for them and guides them to the straight method:

﴿If only they had been content with what God and His Messenger gave them, and had said, "God is sufficient for us; God will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger; to God we are turning," [it would have been better for them].﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 59): that is, taking the means that lead to Him. Whoever desires the love of God must desire the path that leads to Him. Then the father of Abraham says:

﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾ (Surah Maryam, 46): that is, you must abandon this matter to which you are calling. Stoning is pelting with stones, and it seems that stoning was a method of severe torture, as in the Most High's words:

﴿If they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you or return you to their creed﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 20). ﴿And leave me for a long time﴾ (Surah Maryam, 46): that is, keep away from me and part from me. ﴿A long time﴾ (Surah Maryam, 46).

Mulayyan (ملي): a long span of time. From it comes mala'wah: a long period of time; and al-mulawan: the night and the day.

So what did the Prophet of God Abraham say to his uncle after this harshness? Abraham did not depart from his just bearing, and did not transgress the etiquette of dialogue and of calling to God with wisdom and fair admonition.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 19, verse 47:

It seems that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) wished to draw his uncle's attention and to affirm to him that he was in great danger, one that deserves punishment from God. This was something that saddened him and did not please him. How could he leave his uncle without taking him by the hand? So he said to him first:

﴿Peace be upon you.. 47﴾ (Surah Maryam): That is: peace from me, myself. It is a peace that I set against what has come from you. My attitude toward you is peace. I will not answer you with the like of what you said, I will not be harsh with you, no harm will reach you from me, and I will not say to you, "Uff."

But peace from me alone is not sufficient. There must also be peace for you from Allah, the Exalted, because you have fallen into a grave matter that is not forgiven and that deserves punishment, and I fear that you will not have peace from Allah. Therefore he said after it:

﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you.. 47﴾ (Surah Maryam):

It is as if he is apologising for his words, "Peace be upon you":

For I only said to you, "Peace be upon you," while intending to ask my Lord to forgive you, so that peace may be complete for you if you give up your belief in worshipping idols. By this he wishes to soften him and win over his heart.

Then he reported the seeking of forgiveness in the future tense, and did not say "I have asked forgiveness," but rather ﴿I will ask..﴾ (Surah Maryam). He wishes to clear his seeking of forgiveness for his uncle of flattery, hypocrisy and deception, and perhaps if I had asked forgiveness for you now you would think that I was flattering you. As for ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you..﴾ (Surah Maryam), that is: away from you, so that it is a supplication in absence, and it is more likely to be accepted by Allah. Then he says: ﴿Indeed, He has ever been to me gracious.. 47﴾ (Surah Maryam): He wishes to reassure his uncle that he has a standing with Allah, so that when his Lord forgives him, He, the Exalted, will accept from him.

Ḥafiyy (ḥafī, "gracious"): from the verb ḥafiya, yaḥfā, like raḍiya, yarḍā, and it is followed by a prepositional particle that specifies its meaning. You say: ḥafiya bihi, that is, he showed great honour to him, honour that fulfils the requirements of his happiness, and he received him with ḥafāwa, that is, with the honour that suits what achieves happiness for him.

This is a relative matter that differs among people. Some people are welcomed simply by your receiving them even on a mat, and by offering them even a cup of tea, while other people need decorations, luxurious furnishings and sumptuous tables to feel welcomed.

We also say: ḥafiya ʿanhu, that is, he was thorough in searching for him to learn his news, and reached a point of such effort that it wearied and exhausted him. In the colloquial, they say: "I reached him after I had exhausted myself." From this is His saying, the Exalted, concerning the Hour:

﴿They ask you about the Hour, as if you were ḥafiyy about it. Say: its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know.. 187﴾ (Surah al-A'raf): That is: as if you were concerned with the Hour, eager to inquire about it, constantly speaking about its affair. Thus the meaning of:

﴿Indeed, He has ever been to me gracious.. 47﴾ (Surah Maryam) is: my Lord shows great honour to me, honour that achieves my happiness, and among my happiness is that Allah forgives you the great sin you persist in. It is as if he, peace be upon him, magnifies two matters: he magnifies the sin into which his uncle has fallen, which is disbelief in Allah, and he exalts the Lord whom he will ask to forgive his uncle, in His sight. ﴿Indeed, He has ever been to me gracious.. 47﴾: And since my Lord is gracious to me, He will not forsake me. How could He, when He has made me a prophet and has honoured me? So be reassured: if you repent of the false beliefs you hold, He will forgive you. It is as if Ibrahim, peace be upon him, is affirming to his uncle his standing with his Lord, and all his uncle has to do is listen to his words and respond to his call.

Ibrahim, peace be upon him, continued to ask forgiveness for his uncle as he had promised, until it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, whereupon he withdrew from him and disowned him, as Allah, the Exalted, said:

﴿And the request for forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him.. 114﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah).

al-I'tizal (withdrawal, leaving a companionship in favour of something better, even if only in one's own belief). Here the Almighty draws our attention to the fact that when a person debates a matter and sees in his opponent stubbornness and obstinacy in falsehood, he should not prolong the conversation with him, lest it entrench obstinacy in him and move him to the pride of victory, even through falsehood.

Therefore, the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, instructs those contemporary with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that if they wished to investigate his affair, whether truthfully or falsely, God forbid, they should investigate it in twos or individually, and not as a mass, clamorous investigation; for mob action is far from objectivity, in which the individual hides within the crowd, and something may happen whose consequences are not praiseworthy and which no one will know about.

Mob behaviour is not governed by reason or logic, and the crowd, as they say, "its reason is in its ears." We have previously mentioned that when Cleopatra and her ally were defeated, they portrayed this defeat as a victory, as has happened often throughout history, and in this the poet says:

"You hear the people's clamour, the air filled with chanting,
the effect of slander upon them. Oh, what a parrot!
How are they inspired to take the life of their own slayer?
The lie was passed off upon him, and his reason is in his ears."

Thus the multitude does not express a sound opinion, nor does it arrive at what is right. The Almighty says to the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):
