﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up for Allah in twos and individually, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion.﴾ (Surah Saba', 46)

So investigating such a matter requires two persons who exchange views, reasoning and evidence, and who examine the question thoroughly. If one of them prevails over the other, the matter remains between them, without a third party who could gloat over the defeated one. Or a single individual may examine it alone with himself, looking at the person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his conduct and character, and asking how he could be mad when this is so. Have we seen in him any signs of madness? And those who said of him, "He is a sorcerer," why did he not bewitch them as he bewitched his followers?

Therefore, if a single person turns these facts over in his mind and reviews the different opinions, he would be guided to the truth by himself. Withdrawal is thus a required course when a person finds the environment unsuitable for debating falsehood against truth, so that we do not entrench contention and obstinacy in the soul of the opponent.

Therefore the Most High says:

﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] will say: "In what condition were you?" They will say: "We were oppressed in the land." They will say: "Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could emigrate therein?"﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 97)

That is: the opportunity was before you to leave this place for another part of the wide earth of Allah. It is as though the Almighty, blessed and exalted, draws our attention to the fact that the whole earth is the earth of Allah. The wide earth of Allah is not Egypt, Syria, or Germany; rather, the whole earth without barriers is the earth of Allah, so whoever is constrained in one place goes to another, and no obstacle prevents him. Does this exist now? Can you breach these barriers, when there stand over them systems and laws for which Allah has sent down no authority?

Therefore the Blessed and Most High says:

﴿And the earth He has laid out for all creatures.﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 10)

That is: the earth is yours; the earth is for all creatures, every creature. This is among the principles the Creator, glorified is He, established for humanity. When man invented barriers and boundaries, erected walls and wires, and prevented the creatures from moving in the earth of Allah, great corruption arose in the universe. If a place constrains you and you find no alternative elsewhere, and if you live in an environment not sound in its make-up, it is decreed that you will suffer in it all your life.

We have said that these boundaries and barriers have produced a land without men and men without land; were these capacities combined, the world would be set right. As for this matter of withdrawal, or emigration from the land of falsehood or from an environment in which truth does not prevail, it is recorded in several texts concerning our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him), among them the saying of the Most High:

﴿They said: "Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act." We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim." And they intended for him a plot, but We made them the greatest losers. And We delivered him and Lut to the land which We had blessed for the worlds.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 68–71)

So Ibrahim left the land which resisted the method of Allah for another land, and emigrated with his call to an environment suited to it, the land of al-Sham.

Returning to Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) withdrawal from his people: it was not for seeking livelihood and ease of living, but withdrawal for the sake of Allah and in the cause of a faith-based principle to which he called:

﴿O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees?﴾ (Surah Maryam, 42)

﴿O my father, do not worship Satan.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 44)

Analogy would require him to say: "I will withdraw from you and what you worship, and I will worship my Lord." That is: "I will worship Him." However, he turned away from "worship" here and said:

﴿And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 48)

Why?

They said: because a person turns away from his Lord and from His oneness, may He be exalted, only when he is self-sufficient. But when events afflict him and circumstances compel him, he finds no refuge except Allah, and so he calls upon Him. Therefore worship will certainly lead to supplication, and since you will inevitably be driven to supplication, let it be from the very beginning: ﴿And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon other than Allah.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 48)

So he used supplication in place of worship, because I worship Allah in ease, and if hardship befalls me, I have none to call upon but Him. As for his saying ﴿And I will call upon my Lord; perhaps I will not be unblessed in my supplication to my Lord﴾ (Surah Maryam, 48), that is: perhaps I will not be wretched because of my supplication to my Lord, for He, blessed and exalted, does not make wretched one of His servants who calls upon Him. If you want the opposite, then say: the wretched one is he who neither worships Allah nor calls upon Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 49:

His saying:

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob... 49﴾ (Surah Maryam).

Ismail is not mentioned here, because Isaac came as a reward from God to Ibrahim for his patience in the matter of the sacrifice of Ismail, and for what happened of their entrusting the matter to God, the Exalted, and their submission to His decree and His predestination. As God the Exalted said:

﴿So when they had both submitted, and he had put him down upon his face, 103﴾ (Surah al-Saffat). That is: Ibrahim and Ismail. ﴿And We called to him, "O Ibrahim, 104 you have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. 105 Indeed, this was the clear trial. 106 And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice. 107﴾ (Surah al-Saffat).

The matter did not stop at the ransom, but ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Isaac... 112﴾ (Surah al-Saffat).

When he complied with God's command regarding the first son, We gave him the second. In another verse God the Exalted says:

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made each of them righteous. 72﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya): as if the grandson was an additional gift and an increase in the bestowal of offspring, and an exaggeration in honour. Then God bestows favour on all of them by making them prophets, ﴿And We made each of them a prophet. 49﴾ (Surah Maryam). So the favour is not in His giving him Isaac and, after him, Jacob, but in His making them prophets. This came as good tidings to Ibrahim, and his share was to tend the call of God while alive, and to hope that it would continue in his descendants after him. This was also the notion of Zakariya, peace be upon him. All of them are eager for offspring not for glory, multiplication and the inheritance of the goods of this world, but to bear the method of God and to extend the call among them and to carry out its duty.

Consider His saying, the Exalted, concerning Ibrahim, peace be upon him:

﴿And when Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them... 124﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah). That is: He bore legislative duties, carried them out in the most complete manner and performed them in their correct form. So when God knew of his passion for obligation, He completed them for him:

﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. 124﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah). Thus the question of leadership (imamah) arose in the soul of Ibrahim, and he hoped that it would be in his descendants after him, so he said: ﴿And from my descendants... 124﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, corrected Ibrahim's notion of leadership and laid down its general principle: it is not an inheritance; it is a duty with conditions:

﴿He said, "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers." 124﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah). So wrongdoers are not fit for this task. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, absorbed this lesson, took this principle, and wished to be cautious about it in his later supplication to his Lord. When he called upon his Lord:

﴿And when Ibrahim said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits... 126﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah):

he was cautious lest there be wrongdoers in his land, so he said: ﴿Whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day... 126﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

But Ibrahim's analogy here was misplaced, so God corrected the matter for him, because he was speaking of a matter specific to the bounty of lordship (ʿata' al-rububiyyah), which encompasses the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. God guaranteed provision to all, so there is no need for caution regarding the bounty of lordship. Therefore his Lord answered him:

﴿He said, "As for one who disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination." 126﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

So then: there is a difference between the two bestowals: the bestowal of lordship (rububiyyah) and the bestowal of divinity (uluhiyyah), and leadership (imamah) in God's method. The bestowal of lordship is provision granted to all, subject to causes; whoever takes its causes obtains from it what he wishes. As for the bestowal of divinity, it is obligation, obedience and worship.

God the Exalted says:

﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter. 20﴾ (Surah al-Shura).

The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 50:

His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And of Our mercy.. 50﴾ (Surat Maryam).

The intended meaning of "mercy" here is prophethood (nubuwwah). For this reason, when the people of rank and standing among the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from one of the two towns? 31﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf),

it was as if they regarded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as too insignificant to hold this station. The Qur'an answered them: ﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? 32﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf).

So, Allah's giving in prophethoods is a mercy which He spread among the descendants of Ibrahim (Abraham). His saying:

﴿And We granted them a tongue of truth, elevated 50﴾ (Surat Maryam): that is, a word of truth and certainty, conforming to reality. A "tongue of truth" means praise in its proper place and commendation that is due, without flattery. Commendation is made by the tongue. Here we mention this line of prophets, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Is'haq and Ya'qub, with good praise and a righteous conduct, and we take them as exemplars, and all of this is from the "tongue of truth." It appears that this is the supplication of Ibrahim when he said:

﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous 83, and make for me a tongue of truth among the later generations 84﴾ (Surat al-Shu'ara').

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 51:

This too is one of the lines of the prophets. The story of Musa (peace be upon him) has taken up a great deal of space in the Book of Allah, more than the story of any other prophet, which has led people to ask about the reason for this. Even the Children of Israel take pride over other people on the grounds that they are the nation with the most prophets, and this is out of their foolishness, for it counts against them rather than in their favour. The large number of prophets among them is evidence of their obstinacy and their arrogance towards their prophets.

No nation has bewildered its prophets and harmed them as the Children of Israel did, and therefore their prophets were many. The prophets are the physicians of values and the healers of their diseases, so their multiplicity is evidence that the disease has spread, and that it has become a stubborn illness that needs not one physician to treat it, but a team of doctors.

Some think that the story of Musa in the Qur'an is merely a tale of history, as we say and narrate: "Once upon a time such-and-such happened." Had the story of Musa in the Qur'an been merely a historical account, it would have come only once. But it is not so, because the wisdom in relating it to the Messenger of Allah is as Allah, the Exalted, said:

﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the messengers is that by which We strengthen your heart.. " 120 "﴾ (Surah Hud).

Therefore, the purpose of this narration is to strengthen the Prophet (ﷺ) in his call to his people, for he would face many positions and hardships in which he would need strengthening, consolation and comfort. Whenever a matter became serious between him and his people, his Lord would say to him: Remember Musa when he did such-and-such, and you are the seal of the messengers, you are the crown among them, so you must bear patiently and be steadfast.

Had such a story been revealed only once, the strengthening through it would have happened only once, and how many are the events in the life of the call that require strengthening!

Therefore we find the opponents of Islam accusing the noble Qur'an of repetition in the story of Musa (peace be upon him), and this is evidence of their deficiency in understanding the Qur'an. Those places in which they see repetition are nothing but different snapshots of one subject, but each snapshot has its own place and its own birth, so when its place comes and its time arrives, it is revealed.

Among what they saw as repetition, but which is not so, is the saying of Allah, the Exalted, about Musa (peace be upon him) as a child: ﴿an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.. " 39 "﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha).

We ask: when does enmity flare up between two enemies? If the enmity comes from one side, the other side confronts it with objectivity and without obstinacy in the dispute, until the enmity between them subsides; he is an enemy without enmity, so when the one who holds the enmity sees him with this character, he turns away the enmity he has within himself, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Repel with that which is better, and thereupon the one between you and him enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend " 34 "﴾ (Surah Fussilat).

But if the enmity is between two genuine enemies, this one an enemy and that one an enemy, here enmity flares up, its fire grows, a conflict rages between them, and one of them must overcome the other.

When Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, spoke about Musa and Pharaoh, He made the enmity come once from Musa, in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up to be for them an enemy and a grief.. " 8 "﴾ (Surah al-Qasas).

So the enmity here is from Musa, so that Allah might expose the affair of Pharaoh: here he takes Musa and raises him, while he does not know that he is his enemy, and at his hands will be his end, drowned. The standards with him are mistaken, and he claims divinity. And once again He establishes enmity from Pharaoh, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Let him be taken by an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.. " 39 "﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha):

So the enmity here is from Pharaoh. Therefore the enmity is from both sides, and so the battle between them was fierce. Likewise, among the places in which they thought there was repetition is the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿And We inspired to the mother of Musa, "Nurse him; and when you fear for him, then cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers." " 7 "﴾ (Surah al-Qasas).

And in another verse, the Blessed and Exalted says:

﴿When We inspired to your mother what is inspired, "Cast him into the coffer and cast it into the river, and let the river throw it onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.." " 39 "﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha).

The orientalists have made an uproar over these verses, because they do not understand the style of the Qur'an and do not possess the Arabic faculty for receiving from Allah. There is a difference between the two contexts. The first statement: ﴿when you fear for him, then cast him into the river.. " 7 "﴾ (Surah al-Qasas).

These are events that have not yet occurred; they will happen in the future, and the speech is merely the preparation of Musa's mother for the events before they take place.

As for the second meaning, it is direct to the events at the time they occur; therefore it came in concise phrases, like decisive telegrams, to suit the reality of the events: ﴿that you cast him into the coffer, then cast it into the river.. " 39 "﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha).

Likewise the first verse mentioned: ﴿then cast him into the river.. " 7 "﴾ (Surah al-Qasas).

And it did not mention the coffer, as in the other verse: ﴿that you cast him into the coffer, then cast it into the river.. " 39 "﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha).

Thus, there is no repetition in the matter as the malicious claim; each of them speaks of a particular situation and a stage of the story. Then the Exalted says:

﴿And mention in the Book Musa; indeed, he was chosen (mukhlaṣan).. " 51 "﴾ (Surah Maryam).

Takhlīṣ (purification, sincerity) means to extract something from things with which it was mixed, as we extract perfumes from flowers, for one takes the good and leaves the bad. As for a human being, we say: so-and-so is mukhlaṣ, because the human being is composed of multiple faculties, each serving every movement in life, and each of his faculties or organs has a task it performs; yet things may enter into them that are not part of their task, or they may stray from their purposes, so impurities occur in him, and the human being needs to purify himself of these impurities.

For example, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made the coming together of man and woman for a specific purpose, which is the continuation of the species. Therefore, you find that an animal governed by instinct rather than by reason and choice, when both the male and the female fulfil this task, the female cannot be made to allow the male to approach her, and likewise the male does not approach the female if he knows from her scent that she is pregnant.

So the animal, by this instinct, stops at its task, which is the preservation of the species, but man has not stopped at the limits of this instinct; rather, he has made it a personal pleasure, with the preservation of the species coming as a consequence of it.

The same applies to the instinct of food. When a human being is hungry, his instinct requires him to eat, and the wisdom in that is the sustaining of life, not being filled with flesh and fat. The animal stops at the limit of this instinct, so when it is satisfied you cannot force it to eat one more stalk of clover beyond what it has eaten.

As for man, the matter is entirely different: he eats until he is full, then until he is stuffed, and after that there is no objection to sweet drinks and the like. Therefore the Creator, glorified and exalted, set for us the method that regulates this instinct, and said, the Exalted: ﴿And eat and drink, but do not be excessive.. " 31 "﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

And in the noble hadith: "The son of Adam needs only a few morsels to keep his spine upright. If he must do more, then a third for his food, a third for his drink, and a third for his breath."

Among the instincts also is the instinct of curiosity. A person loves to know what is with others, so that the progress necessary for the movement of life may take place among people, and so that the secrets of Allah in the universe may be known. This is the acceptable limit. But if the love of curiosity turns into spying and tracking the faults of others, this is not accepted and is counted among the impurities of souls, and one needs to purify oneself of it.

Therefore, every instinct has a wisdom and a function from which we must not stray. The mukhlaṣ is the one who stops his instincts at their limit, does not overstep it, and purifies them from the impurities that surround them. This quality is either one that Allah honours a servant with, so that He purifies him from these impurities from the very beginning, or one he strives for himself, purifying himself of its impurities by following the method of Allah. This is the mukhlaṣ: the one who has purified himself.

Therefore, they say: among people are those who reach from obedience to Allah the honour of Allah, and among people are those who reach from the honour of Allah obedience to Allah. Allah, the Exalted, made the prophets mukhlaṣīn (purified) from their beginning, so that they would be ready to guide people, and not waste their time purifying themselves from the impurities of life and its trials.

Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not continue for twenty-three years teaching people how to purify themselves? How then if the Prophet himself were in need of purifying himself? And because of the rank and station of these purified ones, Iblis observed good manners and respected this station when he said:

﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, " 82 " except Your chosen servants among them." 83 "﴾ (Surah Sad): because Iblis cannot mislead these people. Then the Exalted says:

﴿And he was a messenger and a prophet.. " 51 "﴾ (Surah Maryam): because among the servants of Allah there are those who are mukhlaṣ without being a prophet or messenger, such as the righteous servant (al-'abd al-salih), for example. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, informed us about Musa (peace be upon him) that He had gathered all these qualities for him.

A messenger (rasul) is one to whom a law is revealed that he acts upon and is commanded to convey to his people. A prophet (nabi), on the other hand, is one to whom a law is revealed that he acts upon, but he is not commanded to convey it.

Therefore, every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger, because the prophet lives by the method of the messenger who is contemporary with him or who preceded him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 52:

His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And We called him from the right side of the Mount.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:52)

Is it the right side of the Mount, or the right side of Musa? A place is not called "right" or "left" in itself. Right and left are relative to you or to someone else: what you consider right, another considers left. A place is described as right or left only when you measure it against a fixed point, such as the qiblah. So you say: the right of the qiblah, the left of the qiblah, behind the qiblah, in front of the qiblah.

Therefore, His saying, ﴿from the right side of the Mount﴾, means: the right side of Musa, while he was facing the mountain. This is a brief excerpt from the story, which came in detail in His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he perceived a fire from the side of the Mount.﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 28:29)

And His saying: ﴿and We brought him near as a confidant.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:52) means: We brought him near so that We might speak to him confidentially. The najiy (confidant) is the one who speaks privately to his companion, as the noble hadith says: "When there are three of you, two should not confide together apart from the third, for that would grieve him."

God Exalted brought Musa near to converse with him, because this is a distinction specific to Musa, peace be upon him. God's speech to Musa was particular to him alone, and no one else heard it. If you say: how then does God speak to him with speech, and it is called confidential conversation? They said: because He, Exalted is He, let Musa hear it and hid it from others, so it became a confidential conversation, as two people speak together in secret. This is part of the perfection of His power, that He causes this to be heard and that not to be heard.

Some exegetes hold that al-Ayman (the right) is not from "right," but from "yumn" (blessing and good fortune). As for ﴿We brought him near﴾: it means from the presence of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He. But is it the Truth who drew near to him, or Musa who drew near to the presence of the Truth, glorified is He? How can we say that God drew near to him, when He, glorified is He, is nearer to him than his jugular vein? So the drawing near is for Musa, peace be upon him.

Thus the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, gathered for Musa several qualities: He made him a sincere servant, a messenger and a prophet, and singled him out with speech and confidential conversation.

God granted Moses his brother Aaron (Harun) as a mercy to Moses, because Aaron was a helper to his brother and a supporter for him in the matter of the call (da'wah). Such a thing did not happen with any other prophet, that God should appoint for him a helper in bearing this mission. Therefore Moses, peace be upon him, said:

﴿And my brother Aaron — he is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a helper, to confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 28:34)

And ridf (ردء) is: the helper. Thus the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has given us a quick glimpse of the procession of prophethood in the story of Moses, and a brief flash here whose detail has come in another place.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 19, verse 54:

Allah the Exalted says:

﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise…﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:54):

What is the distinction here, since all the messengers were true to their promises? They said: Because there is a quality that stands out in a person and distinguishes him by it, even if it exists in others. The one who is truthful in a promise he has made, or a word he has spoken, is truthful in a matter that he controls and that concerns him.

As for Isma'il (peace be upon him), he was true to his promise in a matter of life or death, a matter that concerned himself, when he said to his father:

﴿O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the steadfast﴾ (Surah al-Saffat 37:102).

Would that the matter had come directly, but it was seen by another. Perhaps the matter would have been easier if the son had seen his father slaughtering him; but it was a dream that the father saw, and a dream does not establish a ruling except for the prophets. So Isma'il was precise in his reply when his father informed him, as if he were seeking his opinion on this matter:

﴿Indeed, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so consider what you see…﴾ (Surah al-Saffat 37:102).

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) feared that his son would submit to being slaughtered without being told, lest a time come when the son would be filled with resentment toward his father, if he did not know the reason. So Ibrahim wished that his son's submission to being slaughtered would be a means of drawing near to Allah, for which he would have its reward and recompense.

Isma'il (peace be upon him) said to his father Ibrahim:

﴿O my father, do as you are commanded…﴾ (Surah al-Saffat 37:102).

The promise in which he was truthful was his saying:

﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, among the steadfast﴾ (Surah al-Saffat 37:102).

Isma'il was truthful in his promise, submitted to the slaughter, and did not hesitate or draw back. Therefore he deserved that his Lord distinguish him with this quality: ﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise…﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:54).

When the Almighty saw the submission of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both) to Allah's decree, He lifted that decree from him and called out to him:

﴿O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the dream. Indeed, that is how We reward the doers of good. Indeed, this was clearly a trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾ (Surah al-Saffat 37:104–107).

The outcome of this trial was that Allah ransomed the one who was to be slaughtered and freed him from slaughter. Then He honored Ibrahim, beyond the son, with another son:

﴿And We gave him Ishaq…﴾ (Surah al-An'am 6:84).

This is a Qur'anic snapshot that teaches us that when a Muslim submits to Allah's decree and is content with His destiny, he will reap the fruits of this submission. What prolongs the decree upon people is that they do not accept it, and the Almighty is not compelled by anyone. The decree is executed, executed, whether you are pleased with it or not.

When you submit to Allah and are content with His decree, He lifts it from you, or shows you the good in it. So you must respect destiny and be content with it, for it comes from your Lord, the Creator, the Wise, and Allah does not lift His decree from creation until they are content with it.

We often see people objecting to Allah's decree, especially at the death of a young child. They weep and wail excessively over him, and one of them says: "He did not enjoy his youth."

We marvel at such ignorance: What youth? What enjoyment is this? He departed in his childhood from a vain and transient world, a temporary pleasure, to an abode that endures and a lasting bliss. How, when he has left living with creation and gone to the presence of the Creator, glory be to Him?

Indeed, he is in a bliss that, if you knew it, you would wish to be in his place. It is enough that these children are not questioned and not held to account, and they have no private dwelling in Paradise, because they roam free in it, frolicking as they wish. Therefore they are called "the darting ones of Paradise" (da'ami" al-Jannah).

Another objects because a colleague at work was promoted until he became his superior, so he begins to harbor resentment toward him, belittle him, and his soul blazes with anger. Before all of this, he should have asked himself: Did his colleague take anything from Allah's dominion without His decree and destiny? So if you do not respect this colleague, then respect Allah's decree concerning him, for he took nothing by force against Allah.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Listen and obey, even if a slave of Abyssinian origin, whose head is like a raisin, is appointed over you."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 55:

That is: among the great qualities of Isma'il that God Most High mentioned about him:

﴿And he used to enjoin on his family prayer and zakat...﴾ [Maryam 19:55]. That is: his wife. God, blessed and exalted, does not concern Himself with a quality or mention it unless it is great in His sight, equal to being true to His promise and being a messenger and a prophet. Whoever wishes to be characterised by one of the attributes of prophethood must enjoin his family to prayer and zakat.

But why was the family singled out in particular? The family was singled out because they are the immediate environment: if it is made righteous for a man, his house is made righteous for him, and his offspring too. When a man draws his family's attention to the remembrance of God and to prayer five times a day and night, he thereby closes the way to Satan, for he has no room in a house where the family prays the five prayers.

Accordingly, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on a man who gets up at night, prays two rak'ahs, then wakes his wife; if she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face. And may God have mercy on a woman who gets up at night, prays two rak'ahs, then wakes her husband; if he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face."

So every man and every woman can, each night, be a messenger to their family and their environment, performing the task of the messenger; because Muhammad (ﷺ) is the seal of the prophets and messengers, there is no legislation after his legislation, and no book after the writing of the Book; his community will carry his message after him, and every believer among them who knows a ruling of Islam is a successor to the Messenger of God in conveying it.

As God Most High said:

﴿That you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you...﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:143].

The Messenger bears witness that he has conveyed to you, and you must bear witness that you have conveyed to people. Since you have conveyed to people by speech and utterance, it must also be by conduct, for you have in the Messenger of God a good example.

God, blessed and exalted, always pairs prayer with zakat. Prayer takes some of one's time, and zakat takes wealth, which is the branch of work, which is the branch of time. If zakat takes the fruit of time, prayer takes time itself. So in prayer there is a zakat more far-reaching than zakat.

If zakat brings growth and blessing to wealth, and though it appears outwardly as a loss, then in prayer there is growth and blessing in time. So beware of saying: "I am busy and find no time for prayer," for the minutes in which you pray your Lord's obligation are what will spread blessing through your whole time.

Moreover, when you stand before your Lord in prayer, you receive a luminous charge of faith that helps you carry out your task in life, and you present yourself to your Lord, your Creator and Maker, and you will not lack any good that reaches you from this meeting.

Imagine a manufactured thing presented to its maker five times every day: would it suffer a defect or fault? If the engineer who makes it works on material things, that is because it is perceptible and visible; but the Creator, glory be to Him, is unseen, and He sets you right from where you do not know.

And if Isma'il, peace be upon him, used to enjoin his family to prayer and zakat, he was all the more eager for them, by way of priority. As for His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And he was pleasing to his Lord﴾ [Maryam 19:55]. That is: God was pleased with him, not merely because of the good qualities by which He described him, but from the beginning; He was pleased with him, so He chose him as a messenger and prophet.

The Qur'an continues to give us glimpses of the procession of messages and prophethoods. Idris, peace be upon him, was the first prophet after Adam, peace be upon him; he is Idris son of Shaytha son of Adam. After Idris came Nuh (Noah), then Ibrahim (Abraham), and from him came the succession of various prophethoods.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was a man of truth (siddiq), a prophet﴾ [Maryam 19:56].

We spoke about the meaning of siddiq (one who affirms the truth, a man of unwavering truthfulness) when discussing Ibrahim, peace be upon him. The siddiq is one who exaggerates in affirming the truth that has come to him, so Allah grants him, by that, a criterion (furqan) and a radiance (ishraq) by which he distinguishes truth, so that Satan does not clash with him, for Satan may penetrate your mind and mine.

As for what comes from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, Satan cannot oppose it or enter into it. Therefore the siddiq, even if he is not a prophet, is joined to the prophets and the martyrs, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets, the affirmers of truth (siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:69].

Likewise Idris, peace be upon him, was a prophet (nabi), and it was not said "a messenger and a prophet," because between him and Adam, peace be upon him, there were two generations, and so the messenger-ship of Adam was still in force.

"A high station" (مكاناً عالياً) from the heavens: a lofty rank, whether a spiritual elevation or a physical elevation, take it as you wish. But beware of disputing: "How did He raise him?" For elevation is from Allah, the Exalted, and the One who created him is the One who raised him.

﴿Those...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58): that is, those prophets and messengers who have already been mentioned and discussed. ﴿...of the descendants of Adam...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58): that is, directly, such as Idris, peace be upon him, ﴿...and of those whom We carried with Noah...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58): those who came directly after Idris.

﴿...and of the descendants of Abraham...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58): that is, those who came after Noah. The descendants of Abraham divided into two branches.

The first: the branch of Isaac, from which came the majority (jumhur) of prophethood, beginning with Jacob, then Joseph, then Moses and Aaron, then David and Solomon, then Zechariah and John, then Dhul-Kifl, then Job, then Dhul-Nun (Jonah).

The other branch: the branch of Ishmael, peace be upon him, from which came the totality of the jewels of prophethood, namely Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿...and Israel...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58) is the Prophet of God, Jacob. ﴿...and of those whom We guided and chose...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58): those whom We guided and chose, that is, We selected and chosen them for prophethood. ﴿When the signs of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down prostrate and weeping﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58).

Why did He say ﴿the signs of the Most Merciful﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58) and not "the signs of God"? They say: because the signs of God carry a method and obligations, and this is burdensome to people. It is as if He is saying to us: beware lest you understand that God burdens you with hardship; rather, He obligates you only with what makes the movement of your life happy and interdependent, and then makes you happy with it in the Hereafter. Therefore here He chose the attribute of mercy (al-Rahmaniyya).

And His saying ﴿they fell down prostrate and weeping﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58): He did not say "they prostrated," but "they fell" upon their faces quickly to the ground. This is a compelled, natural emotional reaction, in which neither reason nor thought has any part. The one who prostrates can prostrate calmly and orderly, whereas the one who falls does not think about that. This is similar to His saying: ﴿...then the roof fell down upon them from above them...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 26).

This emotional response they call "an impulsive emotion" (infi'al nuzu'i), which arises from feeling (wijdan), and feeling arises from perception (idrak). These are the three manifestations of consciousness: perception, then feeling, then impulse (nuzu'). A human being has senses through which he perceives: the eye, the ear, the nose, the tongue, etc. These are the means of perceiving sensible things. When you perceive something by your senses, you find that it has an effect on your soul, either love or hatred, either admiration or aversion. This effect on the soul is feeling, and from this feeling there issues a movement, which is "impulse."

For example, if you see a beautiful rose, this seeing is "perception." If you are pleased and delighted with it, this is "feeling." If you extend your hand to pluck it, this is "impulse." The Law does not hold you accountable for perception or for feeling, but when you extend your hand to pluck this rose, we say to you: stop, for this is not yours. The Lawgiver does not forbid you and leave you; rather, He forbids you and inspires you with the appropriate solution for your impulse: you must plant its like, so that it becomes yours, or at least ask its owner's permission.

Likewise is the case of one who listens to the speech of God and His Qur'an: he perceives the Qur'an with his hearing, and from this arises sweetness and spiritual rapture (mawajid) in his soul. This is the feeling from which an impulsive emotion arises, so he finds nothing for it but to fall down prostrate before God, exalted is He. The impulse here was not merely outward but also inward, so their eyes overflowed with tears: ﴿...prostrate and weeping﴾ (Surah Maryam, 58). This meaning is addressed in several other places, as in His saying: ﴿Say: Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 107).

The meaning of ﴿upon their chins﴾ (li-l-adhqan): it is an intensification of humility, submission, and complete prostration, for prostration normally occurs first on the forehead, then the nose, but upon the chins, so this is true prostration, not like the pecking of roosters, as some say. Thus, the People of the Book had knowledge of the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), and that he would come with the Qur'an after a gap between messengers, and now they hear the Qur'an; therefore they say: ﴿Glory be to our Lord! Indeed the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 108).

Among the emotional impulses is also His saying about the People of the Book: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflow with tears because of the truth they have recognized...﴾ (Surah al-Ma'ida, 83).

And His saying: ﴿God has sent down the best of speech, a Book consistent and repeating; the skins of those who fear their Lord shudder from it, then their skins and hearts soften to the remembrance of God﴾ (Surah al-Zumar, 23).

Why does the Qur'an's impact affect all these senses and limbs of the human body? They say: because the One who created the human constitution is the One who speaks, and the Creator, glorified is He, when He speaks and when you understand and comprehend Him, He does not address your intellect alone, but addresses every atom of your constitution. Therefore the limbs fall down prostrate, the eyes shed tears, the skins shiver, and the hearts soften. How could it not be so, when the Speaker is God?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 19, verse 59:

His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿Then there succeeded them a succession (khalf)...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 59). That is: the matter did not continue in the state of the preceding speech that was mentioned; rather, after those people came a successor (khalf). And khalf (successors) are the people who succeed a person, i.e., who come after him or come behind them.

There is a difference between khalf and khalaf: the first, with a sukun on the lam, is used to mean the wicked among a man's descendants and children; the second, with a fatha on the lam, is used to mean the righteous. Therefore, when the poet wished to lament the people of goodness who had passed away, he said:

"The men among whom one used to live in their shelter have gone, and there remained among us a later generation like the mangy hide of a camel."

So what do you expect from these wicked ones? There must come after them evil qualities: ﴿they wasted the prayer and followed their desires...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 59).

So: they are a corrupt succession. The first thing they did was to waste the prayer, which is the pillar of the religion and the first of its pillars to be performed.

It is true that Islam is built upon several pillars, but some of these pillars may be waived for the Muslim and are not required of him, such as zakat, hajj and fasting. There remain two fundamental pillars that never lapse from the Muslim under any circumstances: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and the establishment of the prayer.

Once some of our brothers in Algeria asked us: why do we say of one who performs the obligatory hajj, "al-Hajj so-and-so," but we do not say of one who prays, "al-Musalli so-and-so," or of one who gives zakat, "al-Muzakki so-and-so," or of one who fasts, "al-Sa'im so-and-so"?

I said to the questioner: because through hajj the blessing of Allah upon the servant is completed. When we say "al-Hajj so-and-so," this is an indication and an announcement that Allah has completed His blessing upon him and that he has fulfilled all the pillars of Islam. The meaning of his having performed the obligation of hajj is that he is able financially and physically; and as long as he has wealth, he pays zakat; and as long as he has health, he fasts; and he naturally bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and he performs the prayer. Thus through hajj all the pillars of Islam are completed for him.

Then He, may He be exalted, says:

﴿so they will meet Ghayy (error/punishment)﴾ (Surah Maryam, 59).

Those who seek to find fault and wish to enter criticism upon the Qur'an have taken this phrase and said: al-ghayy means evil, misguidance and corrupt beliefs, and these actually occurred from them in this world, for they wasted the prayer and followed their desires; so how can He say "they will meet it in the future"?

But what is meant by al-ghayy here is the recompense of error and its consequence, just as if you said: "The sky rained plants," the sky did not rain the plants; rather it was the water that brought forth the plants. Likewise, their error and corruption in this world are what drew punishment upon them in the Hereafter.

So the meaning is: they will meet punishment and destruction in the Hereafter.

Nevertheless, out of His mercy toward His creation, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has prescribed repentance for them and opened its door to them, and He rejoices in them if they repent. Therefore, those who are characterized by these evil qualities, who wasted the prayer and followed their desires, do not despair of the mercy of Allah, as long as the door of repentance is open.

Opening the door of repentance before the disobedient is a mercy by which Allah shows mercy to the whole society, including the people of desires and deviations; for if we closed the door in their faces, society would be ruined by them, since they would persist in their falsehood and error, having nothing to keep them upright.

Repentance comes from the servant, and it comes from the Lord, blessed and exalted: the prescribing of repentance and its acceptance are from Allah, and the occurrence of repentance in the servant is from the servant. Therefore He said:

﴿Then He turned to them in order that they might repent...﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 118). That is: He prescribed it for them so that they would repent, and then He accepts their repentance; so it is from Allah first and last. Therefore this exception comes.

Conditions of repentance (tawbah) must be observed, and they are: that you abandon the sin you have committed, that you feel remorse for what proceeded from you, and that you intend and resolve not to return to it again. This does not mean that if you relapse your repentance will not be accepted, for you may be exposed to circumstances that cast you into sin once more.

Rather, what is meant is that at the time of repentance you resolve sincerely not to return to it; if you fall into it again, it will be unintentional and without persistence (israr). For if you were to plan the matter, saying, "I will sin and then repent," who can tell you that God, exalted is He, will grant you respite until you repent? Therefore, hasten to it before its time passes.

These, then, are the conditions of repentance if it concerns a matter between the servant and his Lord. If it concerns the rights of people, another condition must be met, which is to restore the wrongs to their owners if they can be restored, or to give charity on their behalf for good causes, intending its reward for those who were wronged, if they cannot be restored.

Then He, exalted is He, says after this: ﴿And believes and does righteous deeds.﴾ [19:60]

The meaning of "and believes," after he has repented, is that the sin he committed has damaged his faith, so it needs to be renewed. This is clear in the noble hadith: "A fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, nor does a thief steal while he is a believer, nor does a drinker drink wine while he is a believer."

At the moment of committing these sins, the quality of faith is removed from the person, because his faith is absent in that moment; for if he had kept in mind faith and what it entails of punishments in this world and the Hereafter, he would not have fallen into these sins.

Therefore He said, "and believes," meaning: renew his faith and restore it after his repentance. Then "and does righteous deeds" [19:60]: so that he may repair with it what he corrupted by committing sins. The result is:

﴿Those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all.﴾ [19:60]

In another place, the reward of one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds is:

﴿Those, Allah will replace their sins with good deeds.﴾ [25:70]

So why this generosity from God, exalted is He, toward the people of sins who repent? They said: because one who has become accustomed to desire and habituated to sin, and has tasted its pleasure, needs great effort in striving against his soul and restraining it, unlike one who has not become accustomed to it. Therefore the sinners need an incentive that pushes them to return to the courtyard of their Lord.

Thus He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Those will enter Paradise﴾ [19:60] without being reproached for what they did, because they were sincere in repentance to God

﴿and will not be wronged at all﴾ [19:60].

To the degree that repentance is sincere, and remorse for it is great, and to the degree that you blame yourself and pour out tears over your disobedience, to that degree you will have reward and recompense, and to that degree your sins will be replaced by good deeds. All of this is by the grace of God and His mercy.

His saying:

﴿Gardens of Eden...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:61): that is, a lasting abode. You may find gardens in this world and the means of comfort, but it is a comfort that passes away: either you leave it, or it leaves you. So all the comfort of this world comes with no guarantee.

The Gardens of Eden are not the dwellings of the people of Paradise. They are rather common gardens that everyone enjoys. The evidence is that God Most High joined the "goodly dwellings" to them in another verse, in His saying:

﴿God has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and goodly dwellings in Gardens of Eden...﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 9:72).

And His saying:

﴿which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:61).

Al-wa'd (promise) is the announcement of good before its time, to encourage the one promised to act so that he may attain this good. Its opposite, al-wa'id (threat), is the announcement of evil before its time, so that the one threatened may be wary and avoid falling into its causes.

Here He chose the name al-Rahman so that those who have wronged themselves through sins may be reassured that their Lord is Most Merciful and Most Compassionate, that if they turn to Him in repentance He will accept them, and that when He promises, He keeps His promise. God Most High has promised us in His Qur'an, so we believe in His promise in the unseen.

The argument for faith in the unseen concerning what has not yet come into existence, beyond the scene we see now, is this: the cosmos we observe was created in an engineered form, with a perfection that nothing surpasses. So the One who created for us this wondrous, harmonious cosmos, when He informs us of another lasting bliss in the Hereafter, we must believe Him, and take what we witness as proof of what is hidden from us. Therefore we believe in the Hereafter with faith in the unseen, out of confidence in His power, Most High, a part of which we have seen in this world.

Then He Most High says:

﴿Indeed His promise is ever fulfilled (ma'tiyan).﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:61).

Since al-Rahman, blessed and exalted, is the One who has promised, His promise must be ma'tiyan, that is, realized and actual, with no doubt about it. His promise, Most High, never fails. Ma'tiyan here is an ism maf'ul (passive participle), meaning "that which is brought" or "reached": it is we who reach it.

Some scholars hold that ma'tiyan means ati ("coming"), so that the passive form is used while the active participle is intended. But the meaning here is clear and does not need this interpretation, because God's promise is certain, the promised good is fixed in its place, and the skilful one is the one who strives toward it and follows its path through righteous deeds until he reaches it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 62:

Al-laghw (idle, vain speech): it is speech that is superfluous and has no benefit. It wastes time and squanders the energy of the speaker and the energy of the listener, and in the end there is no gain from it and no meaning in it.

The discussion here concerns the Hereafter: ﴿They shall not hear therein any idle talk﴾ (Surah Maryam).

If they heard much idle talk in this world, then there is no room for idle talk in the Hereafter. Then an exception is made from the absence of hearing:

﴿except the word "Peace"﴾ (Surah Maryam).

Salam (peace) is not idle talk; it is the greeting of the people of Paradise and the greeting of the angels:

﴿Their greeting therein will be "Peace"﴾ (Surah Yunus).

Salam may also mean safety from the afflictions they witnessed in this world, for in the Hereafter they are safe from them: no defect, no sickness, no toil, no fatigue. However, we favour the first meaning here, namely greeting, because salam in the verse is something that is heard.

If you say: how is salam excepted from laghw? We say: among the idioms of the language is the affirmation of praise by means of what resembles blame. For example, we say: "There is no fault in so-and-so except that he is brave." You would expect that a fault is excepted from faults, but the meaning here is: if you count bravery a fault, then this person has a fault; we have examined this person and found no fault in him, unless we commit an absurdity and count bravery a fault. Thus his praise is affirmed by what resembles blame. Of this is the poet's saying:

"And there is no fault in them, except that their swords
are, by the clashing of the battalions, notched."

Then He, exalted is He, says:

﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾ (Surah Maryam).

The True One, glory be to Him, did not say "upon Us is their provision," but "and for them is their provision": that is, it is a matter that has been established and allotted for them, a settled matter. Rizq (provision) is everything from which one benefits, and in the Hereafter it is according to the measure of its possessor's deeds of good in the world.

Among the mercies of God Most High towards His servants of the people of Paradise is that He removes whatever is in their breasts of rancour (ghill), envy (hasad) and spite (haqd). None of them resents another who is superior to him in rank, and none desires the bounties of Paradise except in proportion to his deeds and station. If he sees one who is higher than him in rank, he finds in himself no rancour towards him, nor spite against him; for the cause of rancour in this world is that you see one who is better than you.

As for the Hereafter, you will see this matter through a different lens, the lens of the pure soul that does not know rancour. God Most High said:

﴿And We will remove whatever rancour is in their breasts, as brothers, upon couches facing one another﴾ (Surah al-Hijr).

If you see one who is higher than you in rank, you will say: he deserves what he has attained of good and bounty, for he used to struggle against his soul and his desire in this world. And the saying of God Most High suffices in describing the provision and bounty of Paradise:

﴿And therein is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf).

And the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Therein is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."

So: in Paradise there are things that do not fall within our perception; therefore there are no words in our language that express this bliss, for you place in language the word whose meaning you have grasped, while in Paradise there are things you cannot grasp and have no knowledge of. Hence, when the Blessed and Exalted Truth wishes to describe for us the bliss of Paradise, He describes it by what we know of the bliss of this world: palm trees, fruit, pomegranates, the flesh of birds and basil.

And He says:

﴿The likeness of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: therein are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ (Surah Muhammad).

This is with the difference between these things in this world and in the Hereafter. It suffices that you know the difference between the wine of this world, with its bad taste and smell and its stealing of the mind, and the wine of the Hereafter, of which God has negated evil, saying:

﴿No ill effect is in it, nor are they intoxicated by it﴾ (Surah al-Saffat).

As for His saying: ﴿morning and evening﴾ (Surah Maryam): how would their provision come to them morning and evening, when in Paradise there is no time, neither morning nor evening, neither night nor day? We say: the Blessed and Exalted Truth addresses us according to the measure of our minds and the measures we know in this world; otherwise, the bliss of Paradise is everlasting and is not tied to a time, as He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Its food is everlasting, and its shade﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd).

And in another verse, God Most High said:

﴿Those are the inheritors, who will inherit Paradise; they will abide therein forever﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 63:

His words:

﴿That is the Paradise...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:63): that is, the one which We show you as a picture of it is:

﴿which We shall give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were God-fearing﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:63): that is, they will inherit it. Was there anyone in Paradise before these, such that they inherit it from him?

Before He created creation, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, knew which of them would believe by their own choice and which would disbelieve by their own choice. He knew who would obey and who would disobey. He did not compel His servants to anything; rather, He knew what would come from them through the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, exalted is He. Yet He, exalted is He, prepared Paradise to contain all of creation if they obey, and prepared Hell to contain all of creation if they disobey. Thus there will then be no crowding and no housing crisis, whether all of the people enter Paradise or enter Hell.

So then: when the people of Hell enter Hell, where do their places that were prepared for them in Paradise go? They go to the people of Paradise, who inherit them after these have been deprived of them.

Here begins the passage on another topic: after speaking of Paradise and its people, the context turns to something that happened to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), namely what occurred to him when the revelation descended. We have said that revelation descends through Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, who is an angel, upon Muhammad (ﷺ), who is a human being.

The meeting of Jibril, according to the law of his angelic nature, with Muhammad (ﷺ), according to the law of his human nature, cannot take place except through the drawing near of these two natures and a process of transformation that must occur in one of them: either the angel descends in a human form, or the Messenger's humanity is elevated to a degree close to that of the angel so that he may receive from him. This is what used to happen to the Messenger of Allah when revelation came to him.

The Prophet (ﷺ) described this transformation, saying: "...so he pressed me until I reached the limit of my exertion..."

The Prophet (ﷺ) would have sweat pouring from his forehead because of what took place in his body of reactions and chemical processes; then, when it passed from him, these symptoms would go away.

Some of the Companions, who used to sit beside the Messenger of Allah while the Messenger (ﷺ) placed his knee upon his knee, reported that when revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah, the Companion said: "I felt the knee of the Messenger of Allah as though it were a mountain."

And if revelation came to him while he was on a mount, the mount would groan (taii'), that is, kneel down from the weight of the revelation. Allah, the Exalted, has said:

﴿Indeed, We will send down upon you a weighty word﴾ (Surah al-Muzzammil).

Thus: the Prophet (ﷺ) would become exhausted after this encounter and it would be difficult for him, to the extent that he would go to Sayyidah Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, saying: "Wrap me up, wrap me up," or "Cover me, cover me," as if he had a fever because of what he encountered from the meeting with the angel and the direct contact with revelation at first.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, willed to make the revelation pause from His Messenger so that he might rest from his fatigue and hardship; when he rested and the weariness left him, the sweetness of what had been revealed remained with him, so he would long for it anew, just as a person yearns for a place he loves, with thorns and the difficulties of the road behind him. Love for a thing produces a process like anaesthesia, so one does not feel fatigue in its pursuit.

We have said: when the revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah, the disbelievers rejoiced over it and said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him," meaning: He has hated him and abandoned him.

This statement is evidence of their stupidity and foolishness, for how could it be, when only yesterday they were saying of him: "A sorcerer and a liar"? In hatred they remember that he has a Lord who withheld revelation from him, and when he invited them to believe in this Lord they said: "From where did he get this speech?"

Therefore, the Blessed and Exalted Allah addresses His Messenger (ﷺ), saying:

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed down your back, and We raised high for you your remembrance﴾ (Surah al-Sharh).

Thus: the matter of revelation was arduous for the Messenger of Allah. Allah, the Glorified, wished to give these people a lesson through a visible cosmic lesson that both believer and disbeliever witness. This cosmic matter is time, which is divided into night and day, and each of them has its task for which Allah created it, as He, glorified, has said:

﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾ (Surah al-Layl). So beware of changing the task of the night into that of the day, or the task of the day into that of the night. Then He responds to them, saying:

﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He hated [you]. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ (Surah al-Duha).

The meaning: if the day is for the movement of life and its continuance, and the night is for rest and stillness, then they are two complementary signs, not contradictory ones. The coming of the night with its stillness does not mean that the day will not come after it; rather another day will come, and the movement of life will continue.

Likewise, if revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah, do not think that it has ended never to return; rather it is a pause in which the Messenger of Allah may rest, like the night in which you rest from the toil of work during the day. From here comes the wisdom that Allah, glorified and exalted, swears by the morning brightness and the night when it is still, concerning ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He hated [you]﴾ (Surah al-Duha).

We notice in this expression the precision of the miraculous nature of the Qur'anic delivery, where He says: ﴿ma wadda'aka﴾ ("has not forsaken you") with the second-person kaf (you), because bidding farewell (tawdi') applies both to one whom you love and to one whom you dislike; but in qala (hatred) He did not say qalaak, because qalan applies only to one whom you dislike.

As for the meaning of ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ (Surah al-Duha): "the Hereafter," that is, the final period of the descent of revelation, is better for you than the first period, because it will be wider, and it will come to you without fatigue or hardship; and indeed, the bulk of the Qur'an was afterwards revealed with ease upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

So it was with the verse we are concerned with: ﴿And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 64).

It is said that it was revealed when the disbelievers said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him," or that it was revealed after the Meccan disbelievers asked the three questions we discussed in Surah al-Kahf, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I will inform you tomorrow," but revelation did not come to him for fifteen days, so this grieved him and saddened him, and then it was revealed:

﴿And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 64): that is, the angels do not descend except by command, and do not depart except by command. Then the Blessed and Exalted Allah says: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 64).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿what is before us﴾ (Surah Maryam, 64): that is, the future.

﴿and what is between that﴾ (Surah Maryam, 64): that is, what lies between the front and the back. So what lies between the front and the back? Between the front and the back there is nothing but you. He, glorified and exalted, is the Owner, to whom belongs the dominion and what is dominated, to whom belong the place and the one who is established, to whom belong the time and the one who is timed. And His saying:

﴿And your Lord was never forgetful﴾ (Surah Maryam, 64).

Would the Blessed and Exalted Allah send a Messenger and then forget him in this way, without support and confirmation? Glory be to Him, exalted above heedlessness and forgetfulness.

**First:** What is the connection between His saying, ﴿Your Lord never forgets﴾ (Maryam 19:64), and His saying in this verse, ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them...﴾ (Maryam 19:65)?

They said: Because this great universe, with its heavens and earth, and the intricate design of its creation and the marvel of its making, subsists by God's *qayyumiyyah* (the attribute of being self-subsisting and sustaining all things) over it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah sustains the heavens and the earth, lest they cease...﴾ (Fatir 35:41).

So do not think that the universe is sustained by a law that runs it, but rather by the *qayyumiyyah* that sustains every affair of the universe. The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep. Since this is the case, and since He, exalted is He, knows what is before us, what is behind us, and what is between that, and since He, exalted is He, is the *Qayyum* who does not forget or neglect, and by Him the universe subsists, then He alone deserves worship and obedience in what He commands. He has bestowed upon you, before He imposed any obligation on you, a bounty that you could not provide for yourself, and then He left you to enjoy this bliss for fifteen years without obligating you to any acts of worship. Therefore, here He says, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be patient in His worship...﴾ (Maryam 19:65).

The Qur'an has affirmed the matter of divine oneness in many verses, that He is one Lord. He said: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them...﴾ (Maryam 19:65).

And He said: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Fatihah 1:2).

And He said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the first ones﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:26). This is because the ancients, such as the ancient Egyptians for example, used to assign a lord to the sky, a lord to the earth, a lord to the air, a lord to the dead, a lord to crops, and so on. Since He, glorified is He, is the Lord of everything, He has made worship follow from lordship (*rububiyyah*). Worship (*'ibadah*) is obedience to the one worshipped in what He commands and what He forbids. And how could we not obey God when we are His creation and His handiwork, eating His provision and enjoying His blessings? In our countryside, a man says to his rebellious son: "Whoever eats my morsel should heed my word."

We must know that God has absolute perfection before He created creation, and with the attributes of perfection He created. Obedience does not benefit Him, and disobedience does not harm Him. If you say: Then why does He obligate creation with commands and prohibitions? We say: God obligated creation so that the movement of life would continue, efforts would support one another and not collide, and so that progress would occur in their lives and they would be happy in them. Were He to leave them to their desires, life would be corrupted, for you build while another demolishes.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Had the truth followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted...﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:71).

So: The legislations were made for our benefit: ﴿So worship Him and be patient in His worship...﴾ (Maryam 19:65).

Because worship involves hardship, it requires patience, for it commands you to do things that are difficult for you to do, and forbids you from things that are difficult for you to abandon because you have become accustomed to them.

Patience is required of all of us; each of us must be patient with the other, for we are children of different circumstances. If you are patient with harm, people will be patient with you if harm comes from you toward them. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿...and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ (al-'Asr 103:3).

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, teaches us: if someone wrongs you or harms you, forgive him, as you would love for Me to forgive you your sins, and pardon your evil deeds. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (al-Nur 24:22).

Do not think that your patience with the harm of others or your forgiveness of them is a voluntary act from yourself, for it will not be lost to you with God, and it will be returned to you in a sin that will be forgiven for you. Even if someone is exposed, for example, or is falsely accused, God does not waste it; rather He stores it for him as a disgrace that He will cover for him. Whoever exposes another for what he did not do, God will cover for him what he did.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾ (Maryam 19:65):

We have previously discussed the meaning of (*al-sami*, namesake), and the scholars differed about its meaning. They said: *al-sami* is the one who rivals you in height, meaning you rise high and He rises above you; or *al-sami* means equal and similar.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has no namesake who rivals Him in the attributes of perfection, nor any equal, match, or likeness, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ (al-Shura 42:11).

And His saying: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent﴾ (al-Ikhlas 112:1–4).

There is another meaning of *al-sami* that we clarified in the story of Yahya, where He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We have not made for him before any namesake﴾ (Maryam 19:7). That is: no one before was named with this name. Likewise, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has had no one named with His name, neither before this verse nor after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) proclaimed it as a challenge to the disbelievers and atheists who dare to insult God. So why has none of them dared to name his son "Allah"?

The reality is that these people, although they are disbelievers and atheists, nevertheless in the depths of their souls believe in God, acknowledge His existence, fear the consequences of such naming, and do not feel safe from harm befalling them because of it.

So: it has not happened, and no one has dared to do it, because God, exalted is He, has said it and declared it as a challenge; and when God says something, He takes the choice of creation, and He knows that they will not dare to commit this act.

What is meant by "al-insan" (mankind)? The word is used to mean all people in general, as in:

﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious.﴾ (Surat al-Ma'arij, 19)

It is also used to mean a specific group of people, as in His saying:

﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ (Surat an-Nisa', 54)

Here, "the people" refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Another example is His saying:

﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it only increased them in faith, and they said, "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ (Surat Ali 'Imran, 173)

Here, the meaning is specific people. The meaning of:

﴿And man says...﴾ (Surat Maryam, 66)

is: the disbeliever who does not believe in the Hereafter and considers resurrection after death unlikely:

﴿"When I have died, will I really be brought out alive?"﴾ (Surat Maryam, 66)

The interrogative here is for denial. However, refuting this matter is easy and straightforward.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 67:

Fulan: a man is restored (to life) from something easier than being restored from nothing. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, says, in clarifying this matter:

﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him.﴾ (Surah ar-Rum, 27)

Although the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is not described as "easy" (hayyin) and "easier" (ahwan), or "difficult" and "more difficult," He speaks to us in terms of what we understand and what we know from our customs.

In our own customary understanding, bringing something into existence from something already existing is easier than bringing it into existence from non-existence. And although the servant's action depends on treatment (mu'alajah) and engaging in causes (asbab), the action of the Creator, glorified is He, occurs simply by His saying to a thing "Be," and it is. In another verse He, exalted is He, says:

﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul.﴾ (Surah Luqman, 28)

When Imam Ali, may Allah honour his face, was asked: How does Allah call the people to account all together at one time? He said: As He provides for them all at one time.

As for His saying:

﴿Does not man remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?﴾ (Surah Maryam, 67)

That is: if he remembered this reality, he would not deny the resurrection. This matter is also addressed in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 78)

Had he remembered his first creation, he would not have struck this example for Us. Then the logical answer comes:

﴿Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation."﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 79)

And here too the proof is:

﴿We created him before, when he was nothing.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 67)

**His saying, may He be exalted:**

﴿By your Lord, We will surely gather them, and the devils...﴾ (68) (Surah Maryam)

Al-ḥashr (the gathering): that God raises them from their graves, then drives them together, gathered, to the Fire, along with the devils who used to lure them into disobedience and make it appealing to them.

﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, kneeling﴾ (68) (Surah Maryam). It is said: *jathā yajthū fahuwa jāthin* (جثا يجثو فهو جاثٍ), meaning he lowers himself onto his knees. This indicates humiliation, submission, and abasement, in which one is unable to stand upright.

**Naza'a** (النزع): to pull a thing out from its root by force. One only says *naza'a* when the thing pulled out is still firmly attached to the thing it is pulled from. Among examples is the words of Allah, Exalted:

﴿Say: "O Allah, Master of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will, and You take the kingdom away from whom You will..."﴾ (Surah Aal 'Imran, 26)

It is as though they were still clinging to it and eager for it.

As for His words, ﴿from every faction (shi'ah)...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 69): that is, groups that follow one another in a false opinion, are persuaded by it, and go along with its adherents.

﴿Then We will surely drag out from every group whichever of them was most insolent (ashaddu 'ala al-Rahman 'itiyya) against the Most Merciful﴾ (Surah Maryam, 69). **'Itiyy** (العتي): one who has reached the peak of tyranny and arrogance, such that no one stands against him. As we said also regarding the description of old age: ﴿And you have indeed reached extreme old age (min al-kibar 'itiyya)﴾ (Surah Maryam, 8), because when old age comes there is no remedy for it, and no one can overcome it.

It is well known that when the heavenly messages descended to the people of the earth, there were people who were harmed by these messages in their persons, their wealth, their status, and their dominance. The messages of Allah came to affirm the truth, to establish the oneness of Allah, and the equality of creation before the methodology of Allah.

There are also tyrants, oppressors, and masters who have slaves. In this world there is the strong and the weak, the rich and the poor, the healthy and the sick, so the messages of heaven came to bring about the abolition of servitude (istitrāq lil-'ubudiyya).

So who is harmed, angered, and opposed by the messages of heaven? They are these tyrannical oppressors, the people of authority, wealth, and influence, and these must have followers who follow them and support them in their falsehood.

When the Day of Resurrection and the Day of Reckoning come, with whom shall we begin? The most severe (al-ankā) is that we begin with these tyrannical oppressors, and we bring these masters forward before their followers, so that they see them humiliated and abased, though they were arrogant tyrants in the world. In this way we also sever the hope of the followers for salvation.

Perhaps they thought that these tyrannical oppressors would intervene and defend them, for in the world they were their servants, their followers, and their supporters. So when we seize them first and begin with them, we have cut off the followers' hope of salvation.

This meaning also occurs in His words, Exalted: ﴿And on the Day We gather from every nation a company (fawjan) of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven in ranks...﴾ (Surah al-Naml, 83).

That is: from among their great ones and tyrants, so that the followers may see the fate of their leaders, and the weak may witness the downfall of the powerful, and their hope of salvation is cut off.

In the Qur'an's account of Pharaoh, who reached the peak of tyranny and arrogance by claiming divinity, Allah says about him:

﴿He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are led﴾ (Surah Hud, 98).
