So he is their leader and their forerunner to Hell, just as he was their leader to misguidance in the world. He was the teacher, and they were the imitators.

Therefore he bears two burdens: the burden of his own misguidance, and the burden of misguiding his people, as in the words of Allah, Exalted:

﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 79).

Ṣaliyyan: iṣṭilāʾan wa-iḥtirāfan fī al-nār (burning and being scorched in the fire). From ṣalā yaṣlā: he entered the fire and tasted its heat. As for iṣṭalā, it means he sought out the fire himself, as in His saying: ﴿So that you may warm yourselves﴾ (Surat al-Naml, 27:7).

The meaning is that We know best who is most deserving to enter the Fire first. It is as if they have known priorities in this matter, because they will dispute with one another in the Hereafter, debate, and blame one another, and there will take place between them a terrible, dreadful scene that exposes what they committed.

So the follower and the followed, and the worshipper and the worshipped, each will cast the blame upon the other. Listen to them as they say:

﴿Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.﴾ (Surat al-Ahzab, 33:67–68)

And in another verse: ﴿When those who were followed disowned those who followed, and they saw the punishment, and their means of connection were severed.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 2:166)

And God the Mighty has spoken the truth when He said: ﴿Intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf, 43:67)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 71:

This is a general address to all creation without exception, as evidenced by the Almighty's words that follow it: ﴿Then We will save those who were righteous...﴾ [19:72].

(Surah Maryam).

So: the coming (al-wurud) here includes the righteous and others.

What is the meaning of al-wurud here? Al-wurud is to go to the source of water for drinking, i.e., to take water without drinking from it, as in the Almighty's words: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found there a community of people watering [their flocks]...﴾ [28:23] (Surah al-Qasas): that is, he reached the water. So the meaning of:

﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it...﴾ [19:71] (Surah Maryam):

That is: all of you, righteous and criminal alike, will be returned to the Fire and will see it, because the Sirat (bridge) over which everyone passes is laid over the back of Hell.

Concerning this, there is the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Sirat is placed between the backs of Hell, and it has hooks like the hooks of al-sa'dan (a thistle). Then people will seek passage. So one who is saved is a Muslim, and one who is torn by it, then one who is saved and one who is held back by it, and one who is thrown down and tumbled into it."

So when the believer sees the Fire from which Allah has saved him, he praises Allah, and knows His blessing and mercy towards him. Some scholars hold that wurud means: to come to the water and drink from it, and they cite the Almighty's words: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire...﴾ [11:98] (Surah Hud):

That is, He will make them enter. But this contradicts the Arabic usage in which the Qur'an was revealed, where the poet says:

*When they came to the water, its clear pools blue-tinged, we set down the staffs of the settled encampment.*

That is: when they arrived at the water they pitched their tents beside it. At the moment they arrived and pitched their tents beside it, they had not yet drunk from it or taken any of its water. So the meaning of wurud is arrival at it without drinking from its water.

Those who hold the view that ﴿...entering it...﴾ [19:71] means entering also cite the Almighty's words: ﴿Then We will save those who were righteous and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [19:72].

They say: if wurud were merely arriving at the place of water without drinking from it or entering it, He would not have said: ﴿and leave the wrongdoers therein﴾ [19:72].

He would have said: "Then Allah will save those who were righteous and cast the wrongdoers [in]..." But: ﴿and leave the wrongdoers...﴾ [19:72], therein is the proof that they all enter the Fire.

According to the first view, wurud means seeing the Fire without entering it, and its wisdom is that Allah bestows favour upon His believing servants by showing them the Fire and its blazing, so that they may know Allah's grace upon them and what faith in Allah has bestowed upon them of deliverance from this Fire, as the Almighty said: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has truly succeeded﴾ [3:185] (Surah Al 'Imran).

The verse may also be understood according to the other meaning: wurud as entering, because the Creator, glory be to Him, created things and created for each thing a nature that governs it, and He alone is able to suspend that nature and strip it of its properties.

As we saw in the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, the entry of the believers into the Fire would be like what happened to Ibrahim, whom Allah made "coolness and safety" for him, and Allah empowered them over him, so they threw him into the Fire, which remained in its nature with the law of burning, and He did not send down rain upon the Fire to extinguish it, providing for them every means of burning; yet He saved him from it so that the miracle would be manifest before their eyes.

And just as Allah removed the nature of water in the story of Musa, peace be upon him, so that it froze and its flow ceased until every separated part became like a mighty mountain, He, glory be to Him, is able to change the natures of things. So there is no obstacle to the entry of the believers into the Fire in the manner of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim"﴾ [21:69] (Surah al-Anbiya').

Then Allah will save the believers and leave the disbelievers therein, and that will be more painful and enraging for them.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿It is a decree already determined﴾ [19:71] (Surah Maryam): al-hatm is that which occurs without doubt, and a servant cannot decree inevitability over anything, because he owns neither the decreed nor the one upon whom it is decreed. For you may say to your friend: "I decree upon you that you visit me tomorrow," while you own none of the means of achieving this visit. Who knows whether you will live until tomorrow? Who knows that circumstances will not change and prevent this friend from coming?

So: you do not decree anything; rather, the One who decrees is the One who is able to control things, such that nothing departs from His will.

If you say: then who decreed upon Allah? Allah decreed upon Himself, exalted is He, and there is no other power that decreed upon Him, as in the Almighty's words: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed upon Himself mercy﴾ [6:54] (Surah al-An'am).

Then He emphasizes this decree with His words: ﴿decreed﴾ [19:71]:

That is: a judgment from which there is no return, and Allah's judgment none can overturn; it is a decisive judgment. For example, when the disbelievers of Makkah said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We worship your god for a year, and you worship our god for a year," they wanted faith and disbelief to coexist.

But the Blessed and Exalted Truth wills to sever relations with them definitively and conclusively, admitting no such middle solutions. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship, nor will I be a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor will you be worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion"﴾ [109:1-6] (Surah al-Kafirun):

The severing of relations here is not like what we see, for example, between two states, each of which severs its political relations with the other, and then circumstances may later lead to reconciliation between them and a return to what they were; rather, severing relations with the disbelievers is a binding and irrevocable severance, as if He is saying to them: beware of supposing that we may restore relations with you again. Therefore the negation is repeated in this surah, to the point that some thought it was mere repetition, because they receive the Qur'an without contemplation.

So the meaning now is: "I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship," and likewise in the future: "nor will I be a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor will you be worshippers of what I worship." So no one will compel us to alter this decision or return to reconciliation. Therefore, after Surah al-Kafirun comes the surah of judgment: ﴿Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One"﴾ [112:1] (Surah al-Ikhlas).

He has no second to alter His ruling. His speech and His judgment are final, a decree already determined, from which there is no return and no alteration.
جثياً: من جثا يجثو، أي: قعد على ركبه، دلالة على المهانة والتنكيل.

This is a dialogue that took place between the believers and the disbelievers. The believers were usually the weak, who could not even protect themselves, and had no standing or dominion to safeguard. God's method came for their benefit and made all people equal: masters and slaves, the strong and the weak.

It was natural that this religion would meet with denial from the disbelievers of Makkah, the people of standing and dominion, and the people of strength who take the best of those around them. The weak, however, believed in God's religion at a time when they lacked the strength to protect themselves. When the word of the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted, was revealed: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs﴾ (Surah al-Qamar, 45).

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "And what would make you know who Umar is?" He asked: "What multitude is this? And what rout? We are unable to protect ourselves!"

At this time, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the oppressed believers to emigrate to Abyssinia and to Madinah. When God's victory and support came to the believers at Badr, Umar said: "Allah spoke the truth: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs﴾ (Surah al-Qamar, 45)."

In this dialogue, the disbelievers reproach the believers in God: "What has faith in God benefited you, when you are in such a state of weakness, humiliation, abasement and narrow living? Would a Lord be pleased that those who believe in Him are in this condition, while His enemies and the disbelievers in Him are the people of standing and dominion and abundant provision?" Thus God tested some of them by means of others, as He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And thus We have made some of them a trial for others﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 53).

So the believer and the disbeliever, the rich and the poor, the healthy and the sick, each is a trial for the other, so that God may refine faith and test certainty in the hearts of the believers. This is because God prepares them to carry His message, (ﷺ), to the whole world in all its times and places. Therefore He must choose for this mission people of strong faith who enter Islam not for worldly gain, but to bear His message and undertake its burdens. This is the trustworthy believer entrusted with carrying God's method.

Among this is what we see: that the methods of falsehood in this world, whoever calls to them bribes the one he calls and gives him. But God's method takes from the one He calls in order to test him and refine him.

How, then, can the rich be a trial for the poor, and the poor a trial for the rich? The rich is tested by the poor, in that he is in ease of living while the poor is in hardship. The rich eats to the point of surfeit while the poor is hungry; the rich wears fine garments while the poor is naked. Will he recognise God's blessing upon him and render its due? 

The poor is tested by the rich when he sees him in this state. Will he be patient in this hardship, or will he object to what God has decreed for him and harbour resentment towards the rich?

If the poor man knew that poverty is a training course conducted for the soldiers of the Truth, who carry God's method to God's creation in every time and place, and that this is God's apportionment among His creatures, he would not object to God's apportionment, nor would he harbour resentment towards the one who has wealth.

Likewise the healthy is tested by the sick and the sick by the healthy. The healthy lives with God's blessing of well-being, while the sick lives with the Bestower, glory be to Him. As came in the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me." He says: "How could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He says: "Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him?"

Therefore you see that the sick among the believers are in pain from their visitors' sufferings, while they are in intimacy with God, which occupies them away from their illnesses and their pains. And who would renounce the company of God? So if the sick man resents the healthy man, he is tested by him, and he should know that if the healthy one is in the company of blessing, then he is in the company of the Bestower, glory be to Him, the Exalted.

After our master Nuh (peace be upon him) had remained calling his people for a thousand years less fifty years, the answer of his people was:

﴿And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us﴾ (Surah Hud, 27).

So the followers of Nuh, in their view, were the dregs of the people. Then they tried to tempt him with them so that he would drive them away, for they were weak, with neither standing nor authority. So he said:

﴿And I will not drive away those who believe; indeed, they are going to meet their Lord﴾ (Surah Hud, 29).

And he said in another verse:

﴿And I do not say to you that I have the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say I am an angel, nor do I say of those whom your eyes look down upon that God will never give them any good. God knows best what is in their souls. Indeed, I would then be of the wrongdoers﴾ (Surah Hud, 31).

Thus, throughout the ages and the variation of the messages, the disbelievers were those whose eyes looked down upon the poor and weak believers, and who tried to drive them out and expel them from their homes. Did the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted, not say to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for them at all, nor are they accountable for you at all, so that you would drive them away and be among the wrongdoers﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 52).

And so came the scene that is before us:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: "Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?"﴾ (Surah Maryam, 73).

His saying: ﴿Our verses, clear evidences﴾ (Surah Maryam, 73):

Al-ayat (the verses): the plural of ayah, which is the wondrous thing spoken of. It is used, as we have said, for the cosmic signs that establish God's power and draw our attention to His marvellous creation, such as the signs of night and day, the sun and the moon. It is also used for the miracles that establish the truthfulness of the Messenger, as in God's saying:

﴿And they said: "We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it in abundance, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claimed, or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 90–93).

And the word ayat is also used for the verses of the Qur'an that contain the rulings, and this is what is meant here, because the verses of the Qur'an encompass all the signs. As for His saying: ﴿The disbelievers said to the believers: "Which of the two groups..."﴾ (Surah Maryam, 73):

That is: we have accepted your judgement on this matter: we, the disbelievers, are in ease, and you, people of faith, are in hardship. So which of the two groups is better in position? And [this is] by your own standards. Thus you are better by your measure; but by the measure of the Most High and the most enduring, it is we. Al-maqam, with a fatha on the mim, is the noun for the place where you stand, from the verb qama (to stand). As for maqam with a damma on the mim, it is from aqama (to cause to stand/reside). What is meant here by:

﴿Better in position﴾ (Surah Maryam, 73): that is, a place in which one stands over the other, i.e., a large house, furnishings, and a gathering-place in which one shows off over others.

﴿And finer in assembly﴾ (Surah Maryam, 73).

A person usually has a house that shelters him and a gathering-place to which he resorts, where he sits with his companions and loved ones. They call it the "sitting room" or the "mandara" (guest reception room), and in it sits the chief of the people with his family and followers around him, as we say in colloquial speech: "he is the centre of the majlis" (the gathering). Therefore, when he rises, the whole gathering disperses, because they are his followers, as the poet said:

"And after you, O Kulayb, the gathering has dispersed."

There is also the nadi (club), which is the place where the great men and notables of the people gather, instead of each having his own private gathering, as we see now: the club of sportsmen, the club of judges, etc. Thus the club is evidence that they are united, cohesive and allied against Islam and against the Truth.

Among this is the saying of the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿Then let him call upon his club﴾ (Surah al-Alaq, 17).

Among this is what was called before Islam "Dar al-Nadwa" (the House of Assembly), where they used to gather to plot schemes against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And some clubs were devoted to the performance of wrongdoing and indecency, God forbid, so they gathered in them for everything evil, such as drinking wine, dancing and indecent acts, as in the saying of the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted:

﴿...and you commit in your clubs what is reprehensible...﴾ (Surah al-Ankabut, 29).

In this is evidence of the spread of indecency and shamelessness among the powerful and their openness about it; they did not commit it in secret, but in the company of frequenters of these places.

Al-nadi or al-muntada (the club, forum) is derived from al-nada, meaning generosity. When an Arab woman praised her husband, she said: "High in pillars, abundant in ashes, near the house to the gathering." The meaning is that his house was the nearest of houses to the gathering-place, so it was the destination of people in fulfilling their needs. Thus the disbelievers' saying to the believers:

﴿Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?﴾ (Surah Maryam, 73) was a cause of temptation for both groups. The believers said:

﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ (Surah al-Ahqaf, 11).

And the disbelievers said: since God has granted us favour in this world, and He is the Provider, then surely they will favour us in the Hereafter. But the verses did not address the opposing response from the believers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 74:

Kam (كم): an informative particle (khabariyya) indicating a multitude that cannot be counted, and that what is said after it has occurred many times. For example, your companion says to you: "You have never done me any kindness at all," so you enumerate for him the acts of kindness you have done for him, saying: "How many times I did such-and-such for you, and how many times I did such-and-such."

Al-Qarn (القرن): the group of people who coexist over a period of time, such that generations overlap among them, so you see the grandfather, the father, the son and the grandson together. They have estimated the qarn at one hundred years. The term qarn is also applied to a group of people who gather around one king or one message, however long their time may be, such as the people of Noah, for example.

Al-athath (الأثاث): this is the furnishing of the house, and this is a matter that is proportionate to the means of its owner.

Al-ri'y (الرئي): on the pattern of fi'l, and it is intended in the sense of maf'ul, i.e., "marra'i" (that which is seen), as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وفديناه بذبحٍ عظيمٍ " ١٠٧ "﴾ (Surat al-Saffat). So dhibh (ذبح) means: madhbuh (مذبوح, slaughtered).

It is also transmitted in another reading: (أحسن أثاثاً وزياً), and this is not far from the first meaning, because zayy (الزي) too is of what is seen, except that it consists of the zayy and the one who wears it. What is meant here is beauty of form and appearance, and the freshness and fine dress of the person, and the disbelievers boasted of this, whereas the believers were disheveled and dusty, wearing patched and worn-out garments.

The difference in some words of the Qur'an from one reading to another has come about because the Noble Qur'an, in its first writing, was written without dots and without vowel marks, relying on the linguistic faculty of the Arab and his eloquence, which enables him to direct the letter according to the meaning appropriate to the context. It remained so until the scholars placed dots above the letters in the Umayyad era. For example, the stroke in the word written without dots may be read from above as nun, ta or tha, and from below as ba or ya.

The Arab, by his knowledge of the positions of words, is able to determine the intended letter. So the word (رئيا) is read (زيا), and the meaning is not far. Among such cases is the word: ﴿فتبينوا " ٩٤ "﴾ (Surat al-Nisa'), which some read as (فتثبتوا, "so verify"). And the word: ﴿صبغة " ١٣٨ "﴾ (Surat al-Baqara), which some read as (صنعة, "craft"). The evidence of their eloquence is that the difference in such letters does not lead to a difference in meaning.

For this reason, the ancient Arab would become angry if a book was written to him with vowel marks, because vocalizing speech was as if it were an accusation of stupidity and of not knowing the language. Hence we find that the scholars who laid down the rules of grammar were not Arabs, because the Arab at this time would disdain to lay down rules for the language, since it was for him a known faculty that needs no study or teaching. As for the non-Arabs (al-a'ajim), when they entered Islam, they could not learn its language except through this study of its rules.

And the Truth, blessed and exalted, says here: ﴿وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا " ٧٤ "﴾ (Surat Maryam).

Because they said: ﴿أي الفريقين خير مقاماً وأحسن نديا " ٧٣ "﴾ (Surat Maryam).

He intends to demonstrate that they are foolish, who do not look at the reality of life to see the outcome of those who were mightier than them in place and standing, and how the matter came to them.

The Truth, blessed and exalted, responds to the disbelievers' claim of superiority over the believers: this superiority is not of your own essence, but is a gift from God and a trial, until when He seizes you, He seizes you in might and dignity, so that it will be more painful, more severe and more enraging for them. As for when He seizes them in a state of humiliation and abasement, that seizing would not have this effect upon them. So Glorified is He, He gives them respite with His blessings so that they aspire to good, then He seizes them, in accordance with the saying of the poet:

As a cloud flashed lightning for thirsty people,
then when they saw it, it dispersed and vanished.

He raised their hopes at the beginning, then He seized them and disappointed their hopes in the end. We give an example of this: a prisoner whose thirst has reached its limit asks for water, and the guard brings him water until it is at his mouth, then as he anticipates quenching, he withholds it from him and deprives him, so that his regret is more intense and his pain greater. Had he not brought him water, it would have been easier for him.

So, when you make a comparison between yourselves and the believers and reproach them with the adornment of worldly life that you have, you have compared the means and neglected the ends. It is foolishness for us to be concerned with the means and forget the ends. So, for the comparison to be correct, compare your state with the state of the believers, at the beginning and at the end.

An example of this: a farmer diligent in his cultivation who tends to it and covers himself with the dust of his land every day, and another who enjoys clean clothes, sitting in the coffee-house and loitering here and there, looking at his companion whom the work has exhausted, and seeing himself as better than him. When the time of harvest comes, the first finds the fruit of his labour and the result of his effort, and the other sits grieving and deprived. So one must take into account, when comparing, the means together with the ends.

For this reason the poet was right when he said:

Will someone show me my goal before my path?
And from where? For the goals come after the paths.

The disbelievers separated the means of the world from the end in the Hereafter, so they boasted and reproached the believers: ﴿أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا " ٧٣ "﴾ (Surat Maryam).

In the story of our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه " ٢٤ "﴾ (Surat al-Ankabut):

Thus they agreed upon burning him, and God saved His Prophet and frustrated their effort. Then the end in the Hereafter was:

﴿وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين " ٢٥ "﴾ (Surat al-Ankabut).

So they should have not looked at the means separated from their end. Here the Truth, blessed and exalted, responds to those deluded by God's blessing: ﴿وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا " ٧٤ "﴾ (Surat Maryam):

And as He said in other verses:

{ ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد " ٦ " إرم ذات العماد " ٧ " التي لم يخلق مثلها في البلاد " ٨ " وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد { ٩ }وفرعون ذي الأوتاد " ١٠ " }(Surat al-Fajr):

The destruction of these and their likes is easy; God requires nothing more than that sandstorms blow upon them, obliterating their civilization and leaving them as a trace after being a presence.

So He calls them to consider history and reflect on the end of their like among the disbelievers and deniers, and what the rank and the assembly they boast of could avail them, and whether these worldly means will ward off from them the end that awaits them in the Hereafter?

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted, does not answer them with theoretical speech saying: "Your end is such and such of punishment," but gives them an example from reality. He addresses His Prophet, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم " ٧٧ "﴾ (Surat Ghafir): that is, of subjugation, defeat and breaking.

﴿أو نتوفينك فإلينا يرجعون " ٧٧ "﴾ (Surat Ghafir): so whoever escapes the punishment of the Hereafter.

And the Qur'an, when it calls them to consider the end of those who came before them: ﴿وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرنٍ.. " ٧٤ "﴾ (Surat Maryam).

It only urges them to take lesson and admonition from those who preceded them, and it reasons from a present reality to the truth of an unseen future. The civilizations that preceded them, and the like of whom were not found in the lands, and whose characteristics were such and such: what happened to them? Are you then stronger than them? Can you prevent from yourselves what befell others among the deniers?

That is the aspect of reality. As for the unseen, the Qur'an presents it in another scene, where He, exalted is He, says: ﴿إن الذين أجرموا كانوا من الذين آمنوا يضحكون " ٢٩ " وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون " ٣٠ " وإذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم انقلبوا فكهين " ٣١ " وإذا رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون " ٣٢ " وما أرسلوا عليهم حافظين " ٣٣ "﴾

(Surat al-Mutaffifin).

This is the scene in the world; so what of them in the Hereafter?

﴿فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون " ٣٤ " على الأرائك ينظرون " ٣٥ "﴾ (Surat al-Mutaffifin).

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted, addresses the believers, saying: ﴿هل ثوب الكفار ما كانوا يفعلون " ٣٦ "﴾

(Surat al-Mutaffifin):

That is: after what you have seen of their punishment, have We been able to requite them for what they did to you of mockery in the world? In any case, their mockery of you in the world is of limited duration, whereas your laughing at them now is an everlasting matter without end. So which of the two groups is better?

So beware that the appearances of things deceive you, or that the glitter of luxury beguiles you; look to the ends and the final outcomes. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا " ٤٦ "﴾

(Surat al-Kahf).

In Surat al-A'raf there is another snapshot from the scenes of the Resurrection, where the people of the Heights say to the people of the Fire: ﴿ما أغنى عنكم جمعكم وما كنتم تستكبرون " ٤٨ "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

Then they turn to the believers in Paradise: ﴿أهؤلاء الذين أقسمتم لا ينالهم الله برحمةٍ " ٤٩ "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

So where are you now in relation to them?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 75:

His saying: (Say) is a command to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension (of time)﴾ [19:75].

(Surat Maryam):

That is, He gives him respite and leads him on gradually (istidraj), because He is the Lord of all. By the decree of His lordship, He gives to the believer and the disbeliever alike. Just as He aids the believer with victory, so too He aids the disbeliever in attaining his aim, as in His Exalted saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [2:10].

(Surat al-Baqarah): Because they were content with it, pleased with it, and asked Him for more.

﴿Then let the Most Merciful extend for him﴾ [19:75] (Surat Maryam): That is, in this world and its adornments, as He said:

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [42:20] (Surat al-Shura).

And in another place He says: Beware lest their wealth and their children impress you, for they are a trial for them, by which He punishes them in this world through striving to amass wealth and raise children, then grief over their loss, and then He punishes them because of them in the Hereafter:

﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the life of this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [9:55] (Surat al-Tawbah).

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour...﴾ [19:75] (Surat Maryam). The punishment: the punishment of this world, that is, the victory of the believers over the disbelievers and their humiliation and abasement.

﴿Or the Hour...﴾ [19:75] (Surat Maryam): That is, what awaits them of its punishment. And at that time: ﴿they will know who is worse in position and weaker in forces﴾ [19:75] (Surat Maryam):

But it is a knowledge that does not benefit, for its time has passed. The situation in the Hereafter is one where there is no opportunity to resume faith, so the affliction here is greater and the regret more intense.

But, what is the connection of mentioning the forces here, while the discussion is about the Hereafter? And what benefit do forces provide on such a day? They said: this is mockery of them, as in His Exalted saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship, apart from Allah, and guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾ [37:22–23] (Surat al-Saffat).

Is taking them to the Fire a guidance?

Then He turns to them: ﴿What is the matter with you, that you do not help one another? Rather, today they are submitting. And they will approach one another, questioning. They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right." They will say, "Rather, you were not believers. And we had no authority over you; rather, you were a transgressing people." [37:25–30] (Surat al-Saffat). That is: we did not compel you to anything; merely when we pointed to you, you obeyed us. Therefore, they will say in another place:

﴿Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and mankind; we will place them under our feet that they may be among the lowest﴾ [41:29] (Surat Fussilat).

We have said that guidance has two meanings: guidance in the sense of pointing to good and explaining its path, and guidance in the sense of help and divine enabling (tawfiq) to faith. Whoever is sincere in the first, Allah helps him to the second. Among the evidence for this is His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ (Surah Muhammad, 17).

And His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿But the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in return﴾ (Surah Maryam, 76). The enduring good deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat): these are the righteous deeds which you did sincerely for the sake of Allah's countenance.

﴿Better with your Lord in reward and better in return﴾ (Surah Maryam, 76).

This is the goal which we await and strive for. So whenever you compare the arduous paths, then pair them with the blissful goal, and the toil of worship and the hardship of obligation will become easy for you.

As for His saying, ﴿and better in return﴾ (Surah Maryam, 76): that is, a place of return to which you come back.

We note here that the Qur'an did not name for us the person who said this statement, nor did it specify him, although he was known to the Messenger of God, to whom this speech was addressed. This is because this statement can be made in our time and in every time; therefore, the important thing is not the person but the statement itself. It has been reported about him that he was Umayya ibn Khalaf, or al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen...﴾ [19:77]: it means: Have you not seen this? As if He is reasoning, from the one he saw, toward this matter:

﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ [19:77]

It is narrated that he said: "If there is indeed a resurrection, I will be in the Hereafter as I was in this world, possessing wealth and children."

Likewise the companion of the garden said to his brother: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [18:36].

A person takes pride only in what is intrinsic to himself, and he has nothing of his own essence; likewise he does not take pride in a blessing he cannot preserve, and none preserves blessings except the Bestower, the Generous, glorified is He. So why be deceived by them?

Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should sink into the earth, who would bring you clear water?﴾ [67:30]

And He says: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if God destroys me and those with me, or has mercy on us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?﴾ [67:28]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 78:

Meaning: Did you say this word voluntarily, of your own accord, or have you looked into the unseen and so know what will be yours in the Hereafter? ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ (Surat Maryam)

That is: Allah the Exalted has given him a covenant that he will have in the Hereafter what he has in this world. So either this or that. Which of these two have you possessed, that you should be so certain of this claim?

This meaning is clear in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Shall We then treat those who submit like the guilty? What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Or do you have a book in which you study? That you will have therein whatever you choose? Or do you have oaths binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you judge?﴾ (Surat al-Qalam)

The intent: Who guarantees for them this that they claim?

Which of these people has a covenant from Allah, exalted is He, that He will not cause them to enter the Fire?

The 'ahd (covenant) is a thing made firm between two parties. A covenant between people is not a trustworthy one: it may be carried out or it may not, because man is a creature of changing circumstances, and conditions may come between him and what he promised. But if the covenant is from Allah, exalted is He, the Owner of everything, with no power able to nullify His will, then it is the true covenant, the trustworthy one, which never fails.

So when you make a covenant with your Lord regarding faith, you cannot guarantee what changes may befall you. But when your Lord makes a covenant with you regarding recompense, then be certain that it is binding and will not be broken.

That is: love and affection in their hearts. And since Allah has given him this covenant, it is a certain fulfilment. He chose here the name al-Rahman because of the quality of mercy (al-rahmaniyyah) it contains, which suits assistance in fulfilling the covenant.

Kalla: a particle used to negate and nullify what was said before it, namely his statement: ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children. Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ (Surah Maryam).

Then what follows kalla is a proof and evidence for the negation. This particle (kalla) occurs in the words of the Exalted:

﴿As for man, when his Lord tries him and honours him and bestows favours upon him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." Nay (kalla)!﴾ (Surah al-Fajr).

So the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted negates the preceding speech, because abundance of blessings and wide provision is not a sign of honour, just as poverty and constriction of provision is not a sign of humiliation. Both are a trial and a test, as the verses have made clear. The bestowal of blessing in itself is not the blessing; rather, the blessing is success in the trial in both states.

For God may give you wealth and you do not spend it in what God has permitted, so it becomes a trial for you and you fail the test. Thus He has not honoured you with wealth; rather He has made it a means of seduction and enticement. In your hand, wealth turns into either a blessing or a curse, and becomes either honour or humiliation.

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿We shall record what he says, and We shall extend for him an extension of punishment﴾ (Surah Maryam).

The word (sanaktub, "We shall record") has come so that He, glorified and exalted, does not hold him accountable on the Day of Resurrection for what he says as if he had done it, but for what was written against him, so that he reads it himself and it serves as proof against him. It is as if writing is not only what we imagine, but a recording of voice and breaths. On the Day of Resurrection each person will find what he did inscribed.

The Exalted says: ﴿Read your book; your own soul suffices against you this day as a reckoner﴾ (Surah al-Isra').

This statement indicates that at the moment a person sees what was written in the book, he will know that it is his own. If we now record our opponents' breaths and words, is it far-fetched for the One who taught us this to record breaths, voices and movements, such that when a person reads and sees them he cannot deny or dispute them?

And His saying, glorified be He: ﴿And We extend for him an extension of punishment﴾ (Surah Maryam).

That is, He increases him in punishment. For extension (madd) means that you increase a thing. Sometimes you increase a thing from within itself, and sometimes you add to it from something else: you may bring a thread and extend it to its end, or you may join it to another thread, and then you have extended it with something from elsewhere. So God increases him in punishment.

Meaning: while he expects that We will increase him and give him, We will take from him.

﴿And We shall inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:80). That is: We will take from him, as in His saying, ﴿Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whatever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:40).

And His saying, ﴿And We were the inheritors﴾ (Surah al-Qasas 28:58).

So it is as if His saying, ﴿And We shall inherit from him﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:80), corresponds to His saying, ﴿I will surely be given wealth﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:77), and His saying, ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:80), corresponds to ﴿and children﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:77).

So he will come to Us alone on the Day of Resurrection, with none of his children with him to defend him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 81:

Alihah (ʾālihah): plural of ilah (god), which is the one worshipped and the Lord who brought you into existence from non-existence, sustained you from nothingness, and took charge of your upbringing. The gift of divinity (ulūhiyyah) is obligation and worship, while the gift of lordship (rubūbiyyah) is blessings and bounties. So then: who is more deserving of your worship, and who has greater right to your obedience?

These people who have taken, besides God, gods made of the sun, the moon, a stone, or a tree: by what did these gods charge you? What did they command you? From what did they forbid you? And with what did they bless you? And where were they when you were a fetus in your mother's womb?

Your father, who raised you when you were small and took charge of all your needs, and your mother, who carried you in her belly and stayed awake for your comfort, are the people most deserving of your obedience, and you may not place any command above theirs. As for others taking possession of you, and having your obedience and loyalty instead of your two parents, this is not permissible, even while you are in the prime of your youth and the height of your strength.

Therefore, among the foundations of upbringing is that parents raise their children upon hearing and obeying them, and that we warn them against obeying others, especially those not entrusted with their upbringing, such as the common people in the street, or bad companions who lead children into what has an unpraiseworthy outcome.

And now we warn our children against walking with an unknown person, or accepting food or drink from him. What we see in our present age makes lengthy elaboration on this matter unnecessary. This, then, is an immunity that must be given to children, just like immunity against diseases exactly.

And so is the case with those who have taken gods besides God and found comfort in a god who imposes no obligation and no hardship in worshipping him, a god who leaves them to worship him as they please. They have taken the gift of lordship and enjoyed God's blessing, but they have abandoned the gift of divinity and so have not worshipped Him, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

Since man is religious by nature, these people chose a religion according to their desires and appetites, and took gods that have no command and no obligation. Among this is what we see from many intellectuals who take the religion of God according to their own whims, and obey the enemies of God in matters far removed from the religion of God, and they are people of culture and mature minds, yet they still convince themselves that they are upon religion and that they are upon the truth.

Then the Exalted says:

﴿That they may be to them a might﴾ [81]

Al-izz (might): it is domination and inaccessibility from others, such that no one can take anything from him. People say: so-and-so is ʿazīz, meaning he cannot be overcome.

And we may ask: what is the might in worshipping these gods? And what will return to you from worshipping them?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 19, verse 82:

Kalla (nay, not so): it negates that these (false deities) have any honor in worshipping other than Allah. Rather: ﴿Nay, they will disavow their worship of them﴾ [Maryam 19:82].

These very deities will disavow the worship of them, and deny that they were gods besides Allah. And more than that: ﴿and they will be against them in opposition﴾ [Maryam 19:82].

That is: at the very time when the disbelievers took them as gods besides Allah and sought honor through worshipping them, they will turn against them and become adversaries and opponents to them.

The ḍidd (opponent) is the enemy who opposes you and who seeks to harm you. In the Noble Qur'an there are many dialogues between these objects of worship and those who worshipped them. For example, those who worshipped the angels and took them as gods besides Allah: Allah asks the angels:

﴿Did these used to worship you?﴾ [Saba' 34:40].

They reply: ﴿Glory be to You, You are our Guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them﴾ [Saba' 34:41].

And the Almighty, Glorified and Exalted, says: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:166].

Therefore the Blessed and Exalted Lord says concerning these: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their calling?﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:5].

So: what the disbelievers thought to be honor and protection became for them opposition and enmity, like the young woman who said to her father: "O father, what made you accept me being betrothed to the son of so-and-so?" That is: what did you find pleasing in him? He said: "O my daughter, they are people of might, of rank and nobility, and people of power and protection." She said: "O father, you had determined that there would be affection between me and their son, but you did not determine that there would be aversion between me and him. If aversion arises, then what you said will become against you, and you will be made wretched by this might and this rank."

Among people are those who take wealth as a god, following the saying of the poet:
"And for wealth there are people: when wealth appears speaking, 'I am wealth,' the people say, 'It is You we worship.'"
And these who worship wealth, who see strength in it and take pride in it, do not realize that it will be for them a burden and a punishment on the Day of Resurrection:

﴿On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard"﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:35].

Thus, the more greedily one clings to wealth, the more it burns him. And you notice in the verse the natural order of the situation of a request, when a poor petitioner stands before a stingy rich man: first, the petitioner's face changes when he sees him, then he turns his face away, then he gives him a coin, then he turns his back on him, dismissing him. In this same order the punishment comes, and the branding, God forbid. The wealth in which he thought there was honor becomes punishment and calamity.

He, exalted, says: ﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will be deniers of their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:6].

Even the limbs that enjoyed your disobedience in this world will testify against you: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur 24:24].

That is because you neglected the One you should never have neglected, and you remembered the one you should never have remembered. The true God whom you neglected now seeks you out and calls you to account, while the false god you took abandons you and hands you over to destruction.

Al-Azz: it is intense shaking, shaking with violence, meaning that they unsettle and agitate them. Similar to it is al-nazgh (incitement) in His saying, exalted be He:

﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah.. " 200 "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

Al-azz or al-nazgh occurs through whispering (waswasah) and enticement (taswil) to stir a person toward disobedience and evil. This meaning also appears with the word tha'if (a visitation), as in the saying of the Blessed and Exalted:

﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when a touch from Satan afflicts them, remember [Allah], and at once they are seeing clearly " 201 "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

And this verse:

﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils.. " 83 "﴾ (Surat Maryam)

raises a question: if Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, dislikes what the devils do to the believing or disbelieving human being, why did He send them upon him?

Allah sent the devils upon man for a task they perform, and this task is trial and testing, as He said, exalted be He:

﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tried? " 2 "﴾ (Surat al-'Ankabut)

Therefore, they carry out the task for which they were created: they confront the believer to turn him away from faith, so Allah purifies the believers through that, and the steadfastness of those who hold firm against the plotting of Satan becomes manifest.

We have said that Satan has a history with mankind, beginning with Adam, peace be upon him, when he refused to obey Allah's command to prostrate to Adam. So Allah expelled him and removed him from His mercy, and Satan wished to take revenge on the descendants of Adam because of what he had suffered at Adam's hands. He said:

﴿So by Your might, I will surely mislead them all " 82 "﴾ (Surat Sad)

And he said:

﴿He said, "Because You have caused me to be lost, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path " 16 "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

Thus he announced his method and his manner: he lies in wait for those who are upright, while those on the crooked path have no need of him to lead them astray. Hence we see him threaten the believers:

﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left.. " 17 "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

It is known that the directions are six, and Satan comes from them all except above and below, because these two are linked, respectively, to the might of divinity from above and to servitude from below, when the servant raises his hands to Allah in humble supplication and when he falls prostrate to Allah. Therefore these two directions are closed to him, because they are directions of obedience and worship, while he only operates in heedlessness, seizing upon it in man.

Whoever reflects on the question of Satan finds that this battle and this conflict are not between Satan and his Lord, exalted be He, but between Satan and man, because when he said to his Lord, exalted be He:

﴿So by Your might, I will surely mislead them all " 82 "﴾ (Surat Sad)

he observed good manners with Allah. Misguidance is not a skill of mine; rather, I will mislead them by Your might, away from Your creation, and by Your leaving them the choice, so that whoever believes believes and whoever disbelieves disbelieves. This is the opening through which I enter upon them, as is evident from the fact that I have no authority over Your people and Your allies whom You choose and select:

﴿except Your sincere servants among them " 83 "﴾ (Surat Sad).

Here too a question arises: if Satan sits only on the straight path to misguide its people, why does he target the disbeliever?

We say: because the disbeliever by his nature and innate disposition inclines toward faith and the straight path, and here is the cosmos with its signs before him, which he contemplates; perhaps contemplation of the creation of Allah will lead him to faith in Allah. Therefore Satan sits for him on this route, the route of thought and reflection, to block him from belief in the Creator, Mighty and Majestic.

Satan incites you either to stir up desire in you or to make you forget an act of obedience, as He said:

﴿And none made me forget it except Satan.. " 63 "﴾ (Surat al-Kahf)

And He said:

﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people " 68 "﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

Many brothers ask: why is it that in prayer in particular the troubles of life and the preoccupations of the world press upon us?

We say: this is a healthy phenomenon in faith, for if Satan did not know the importance of prayer, and that it will be accepted from you and that sins will be forgiven through it, he would not corrupt it for you. But our real problem is that when Satan gives us the end of the thread, we follow it and neglect the saying of our Lord, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah.. " 36 "﴾ (Surat Fussilat)

So when you feel that you are about to slip out of the thread of worship and standing before Allah, there is nothing to stop you except to say: "I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed." Even if you are reciting the Qur'an, you may stop the recitation and seek refuge in Allah from him. And when he sees that you are attentive to his scheming and tricks time after time, he will turn away from you and despair of ensnaring you.

We have previously given an example of this with the thief, because he does not circle around a ruined house but around an inhabited one. When he approaches it, the owner of the house becomes alert and rebukes him, and he flees; the thief may say to himself, "Perhaps the owner shouted by coincidence," and return again. But the owner of the house is awake and alert, and then he flees and does not come back.

We must know that among Satan's stratagems and plots is that when his misguiding you in one door is difficult for him, he brings you to another door, for he knows well that people have keys, and each of us has a point of weakness through which he is approached. Some people are not swayed by heaps of gold, but are swayed by a word of praise and commendation. This accursed one has various "keys" (tafashat) according to differences in personalities.

Therefore it is easy for you to distinguish whether a sin is from the self (nafs) or from Satan: the self stands you before one desire, which you want specifically and accept nothing else; if you try to shift it to another desire, it refuses except what it wants. But Satan, if one sin is difficult for you, calls you to another; the main thing for him is that he snares you.

The Blessed and Exalted warns us against Satan, because he wages war within the human being against his innate faithful disposition (fitrah), which insists that the cosmos has a capable Creator. The proof of the existence of God is an innate proof that does not need philosophy, as the Arab said in ancient times: "The dung indicates the camel, and the footprint indicates the walking. A sky with constellations, an earth with pathways, and seas with waves: does not all this indicate the All-Subtle, the All-Aware?"

Likewise, every craftsman knows his craft and is expert in its finer points and places of defect, so how much more the Creator, Glorified is He:

﴿Should not He who created know, while He is the Subtle, the Aware? " 14 "﴾ (Surat al-Mulk)

So the proofs of faith are innate proofs in which the philosopher and the shepherd share; indeed, philosophy may have come and complicated the proofs. We pause with His saying:

﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils.. " 83 "﴾ (Surat Maryam)

It is known that the work of Satan is hidden, as He said:

﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you cannot see them.. " 27 "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

So how does the Blessed and Exalted address His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on this matter with His saying:

﴿Have you not seen.. " 83 "﴾ (Surat Maryam)? This is a matter that a person does not see. We say: ﴿Have you not seen.. " 83 "﴾ (Surat Maryam)

meaning: have you not known? He turned from knowledge to sight, as in His saying:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? " 1 "﴾ (Surat al-Fil)

The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not witness that event, so how does his Lord address him about it with His saying:

﴿Have you not seen.. " 1 "﴾ (Surat al-Fil)?

This is to show you that Allah's informing you is more truthful than your eye's informing you, for sight may deceive you, whereas Allah's announcement is true and never deceives you. Your knowledge from Allah's informing you is more worthy and more certain than your knowledge through your senses.

The devils: the plural of shaytan, which is the rebellious one among the jinn. The jinn are a creation opposite to humankind. Allah said of them:

﴿And among us are the righteous, and among us are those below that; we were of divergent ways " 11 "﴾ (Surat al-Jinn)

So those below the righteous are the devils.

The Prophet (ﷺ) wished that God would relieve him of the heads of disbelief and the enemies of the call, so God, exalted is He, said:

﴿So do not be hasty against them. We are only counting out for them a count.﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:84)

God wills that their lifespans be prolonged, that their deeds become worse, and that their sins multiply. The scribes (the recording angels) count them and tally their sins. The meaning of ﴿We are only counting out for them a count﴾ is that this matter will come to an end, because everything that is counted comes to an end. As for the thing that cannot be enumerated or counted, it does not end, as in the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿And if you were to count the blessings of God, you could not enumerate them.﴾ (Surah Ibrahim 14:34)

This is because the blessings of God cannot be enumerated, counted, or exhausted. Therefore it was preceded by "in" (إن), which indicates doubt, and it is a matter that no one dares to attempt, because ﴿what is with you will be exhausted, but what is with God endures﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:96).

Here we see the science of statistics (ʿilm al-ihsaʾ) and the advancement it has reached, such that it now has universities and specialist scholars who have applied statistics to everything. Yet none of them has thought of counting the blessings of God in His creation. Why? Because undertaking to count implies the assumption that you can reach an end, whereas they know full well that however much they count and however much they enumerate, they will never reach a conclusion.

Thus, ﴿We are counting out for them a count﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:84) means: We are tallying their evil deeds and counting their sins before their lifespans come to an end. And whenever lifespans are prolonged, sins multiply, and whatever comes to an end by counting comes to an end by provision (al-madad).

The Exalted Lord has given us various depictions and different scenes of the Day of Resurrection. He has given us an image of the false deity and of those who worship falsehood, and of the dispute and debate that took place between the two sides. And He has given us an image of those who cooperated in evil and of those who cooperated in good. Here is another image, presenting the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) on one side and the criminals on the other. So what is the image of the God-fearing?

﴿نحشر﴾: that is, We gather. The wafd (delegation) are the group that goes to a king to receive his gifts; its plural is wufud, and the singular is wafid. This is the condition of the God-fearing when Allah gathers them on the Day of Resurrection as a delegation to receive the gifts of their Lord, blessed and exalted is He. Do not think that they are gathered walking on foot, no. Rather, every believing God-fearing person will ride a she-camel the likes of whose beauty has never been seen, its saddle of gold and its reins of chrysolite (zabarjad).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 86:

And We drive (wanasuq): the driver (sa'iq) is at the rear, urging them on and driving them away, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent pushing﴾ (Surah al-Tur: 13).

He did not say, for example, "naqudu-hum" (We lead them), because the leader (qa'id) is in front, and perhaps one of them might get distracted and stray from him.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Into Hell, as a thirsty herd (warda)﴾ (Surah Maryam: 86).

Al-warud is going to water in order to seek irrigation. As for the Fire, it is the place of blazing flame (al-lazha), the flame-tongue (al-shuwaz), the blaze (al-lahab), and boiling water (al-hamim). So why did He call the arrival in Fire by its heat "warda"? This is mockery of them, as in other verses: ﴿And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal that scalds the faces…﴾ (Surah al-Kahf: 29).

When you hear "yughathu" (they will be relieved), you expect good and hope for mercy, but these people are relieved with water like molten metal that scalds the faces. Likewise in His saying: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ (Surah al-Dukhan: 49).

It is for rebuking the obstinate ones of disbelief and criminality. And from it is His saying: ﴿So give them the tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (Surah Luqman: 7).

Glad tidings are only given for something pleasing. Therefore: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And We drive the criminals into Hell as a thirsty herd﴾ (Surah Maryam: 86) is mockery, just as you say to a careless boy who failed the exam: "Congratulations on your failure."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 19, verse 87:

The disbeliever, when he begins to undergo the punishment, hopes first of all that his deity will intercede for him and bring him out of what he is in. But how far-fetched! Have you not read the words of the Truthful One, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship.﴾ (Surah al-Ahqaf).

Therefore He, exalted is He, says about these people on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿They will not possess intercession...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 87). Intercession belongs only to one who has been granted permission for it: ﴿except one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant﴾ (Surah Maryam, 87).

The covenant that you take with Allah for intercession is that you present of good deeds what suffices for your own obligations, and then add to them what qualifies you to intercede for others. Good does not go to waste with Allah. What exceeds the obligation is in your account, in a Book that leaves nothing small or great unrecorded, and does not neglect even the weight of an atom.

Whoever the believer is, however much he has been wasteful toward himself, when he sees a person turning toward Allah and seeking more acts of obedience, he should pray for him for more, and rejoice for him; for his surplus of obedience may return to benefit you, and you may need his intercession one day. As for those who delight in mocking and ridiculing the people of obedience, as the Truthful One, blessed and exalted is He, has informed: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are the astray."﴾ (Surah al-Mutaffifin, 29–32):

How, then, will you face the people of obedience, and hope for their intercession after what has come from you? If you are not obedient, then at the very least love the obedient and seek their closeness, for this in itself is a good deed for you whose benefit you hope for on the Day of Resurrection.

How similar intercession in the Hereafter is to the intercession that happens between us in this world. When a matter is difficult for you to accomplish, they say to you, "Go to so-and-so and he will settle it for you." Indeed, that person goes with you and fulfils your need. Why, then, was it done by his hands? Surely he has, with the one whose need this is, favours by which he cannot refuse him a request.

So: whoever intercedes must have a store of obedience that permits him to intercede. If you reflect, you will find that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the first to present a store of faith that encompassed his obligation and the obligation of his community. Did not his Lord inform about him, saying: ﴿He believes in Allah and believes the believers...﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 61)? Therefore intercession became due to him, and he was permitted to grant it.

The Truthful One, blessed and exalted is He, never neglects the store of His creatures. Every act of obedience you have offered beyond what Allah has obligated upon you is stored up for you. Even if a person is wrongly accused and punished for an action he did not commit, Allah stores that for him and covers over what he actually did commit, so he is not punished for it.

Thus the covenant in His words, exalted is He: ﴿except one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant﴾ (Surah Maryam, 87), is:

That you enter with your Lord into the station of ihsan (excellence). No one enters this station except one who has discharged what is incumbent upon him of obligation. Otherwise, how can you be a muhsin (one who does good) while you are deficient in the station of faith?

And if you wish, recite the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be among gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them...﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 15–16).

What is the reason?

﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good, who used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness, and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 16–19).

So the muhsin is the one who performs, beyond what Allah has obligated upon him, acts of worship of the same kind as what was obligated. Allah did not obligate us to stand in prayer at night or to seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn, nor did He impose upon us charity for the beggar and the deprived. And we must distinguish here between (ḥaqq) and (ḥaqq ma'lūm): here He said (ḥaqq) alone, because the discussion concerns voluntary charity, whereas the (ḥaqq ma'lūm) is in zakah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 88:

This statement of theirs is folly and fabrication. For when was this begetting undertaken? In which century after the birth of Christ, peace be upon him? This saying did not come about until about three hundred years after the birth of Christ, so what was the position before it? And what was added to God's dominion after this son came?

The sun is the sun, the stars are the stars, and the air is the air. Therefore, the objectivity of this taking of a son is folly, because nothing was added to the dominion through the hand of this son, and there was not in God, exalted is He, an idle attribute that was completed by the coming of the son, because the attributes of perfection of God, exalted is He, exist before He creates anything.

He, glorified and exalted is He, is Creator before He creates, Provider before He provides, Giver of life before He gives life, and Causer of death before He causes death. By His attributes He brought these things into being, so the attributes of perfection in Him, glorified is He, exist before their objects. We have given an example of this, and to God belongs the highest likeness, by the poet who composed a poem. We said: he composed the poem because he is a poet in the first place, and had he not been a poet, he would not have composed it.

Therefore the Truth refutes this fabrication by His saying:
﴿Grievous is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie.﴾ [18:5]

(Surat al-Kahf)

Al- Id (al-iddu): that which is extreme in denunciation and abomination; it is the monstrous thing, from "ada al-amr," meaning the matter burdened him and he could not bear it. Among its uses is the words of Allah, the Exalted, in the Verse of the Throne: ﴿And their preservation does not tire Him,﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 255].

That is, it does not burden Him. But why was this matter made an iddan (monstrous) and a grievous denunciation?

They said: Because taking a child has purposes. A child is taken so that he becomes a support and a strength for you, or so that he becomes an extension of you after your death. Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Mighty, who has no need of anyone, and He is the Everlasting, the Eternal, who has no need of any extension.

So, the taking of a child with respect to Allah, the Exalted, has no cause; and the taking of a child by Allah, the Exalted, negates the equality of servitude to Him, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 90:

Meaning: It is not only we who deny this matter; even inanimate things that are not subject to obligation (ghayr mukallaf) deny it. The heavens, despite their strength and greatness, are "splitting" (tatafattar), that is, cracking apart, and they are almost torn into pieces (mazzan) because of the enormity of what has been said. "They almost split" — but why did they not actually split? They did not split because Allah holds them: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease [to exist]...﴾ (Surah Fatir, 35:41).

In a hadith qudsi: "The heaven said: 'O Lord, permit me to fall in pieces upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld Your gratitude.' The earth said: 'O Lord, permit me to swallow up the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld Your gratitude.' The mountains said: 'O Lord, permit me to fall upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld Your gratitude.' The seas said: 'O Lord, permit me to drown the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your provision and withheld Your gratitude.' He said to them: 'Leave me and My creation. Had you created them, you would have shown them mercy. If they repent to Me, I am their beloved; and if they do not repent, I am their physician.'"

So what is the reason that the heaven almost splits, the earth almost cracks open, and the mountains almost collapse?
This is the cause and the reason on account of which the whole universe nearly quakes and rises in anger at this monstrous utterance.

Here we must distinguish between the negation of an act and the negation of its fitting (inbighā') for the act. For example, in the words of the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, concerning His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾ (Surah Yasin, 36:69).

He negated from him the saying of poetry, and He negated from him that it be fitting for him. Someone might suppose that the Prophet was unable to compose poetry, or that the tools of poetry, such as eloquence of language and delicacy of feeling, were not available to him ﷺ. But the Messenger of Allah is capable of composing poetry if he wished; he is capable of the act, but it is not befitting for him.

Likewise, in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ (Surah Maryam, 19:92). If Allah, glorified and exalted, wished to have a son, that would be possible, as He says, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 43:81).

That is: if He, glorified is He, had a son, then it would be welcome, indeed "upon the eye and the head." But this is a matter which the Truthful, glorified is He, did not will, and which is not befitting for Him. So how could I claim, on my own account, that Allah has a son?

And what need does He, exalted is He, have for a son?

That is because the Creator, blessed and exalted, created man and gave him a sphere of choice: he may act or not act, believe or not believe. Likewise He placed in him a sphere of compulsion. Consider the disbeliever who has become accustomed to disbelief, habituated to it, and rebelled against obedience and faith. Can he, for example, rebel against illness, or rebel against death, or against poverty?

So you are free in some matters and a slave in others. This sphere of choice that you have is in this world, and you do not have it in the Hereafter. We have previously distinguished between 'ibad (servants) and 'abid (slaves). All of them, believer and disbeliever alike, are slaves of God, Exalted is He. The 'ibad, however, are those who have relinquished their choice and their will in favour of the will of their Lord, so that all their conduct comes into accordance with what God wills.

These are the ones of whom God said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility...﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 63).

The meaning of ﴿None comes to the Most Merciful except as a servant﴾ (Surah Maryam, 93) is: in the Hereafter, where the sphere of choice is cancelled, and no one can step outside the will of God, Exalted is He, and sovereignty is taken away from all. God says: ﴿Whose is the dominion this Day? It is God's, the One, the Subduer﴾ (Surah Ghafir, 16). He, glorified is He, is able to give and able to take away:

﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty from whom You will, You exalt whom You will, and You abase whom You will...﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 26).

Al-Ihsa' (enumeration, counting) is the act of counting. In earlier times people used pebbles (hasa) or date-stones (nawa) for counting. But date-stones are a by-product of owning palm trees, so they were not available to everyone; for this reason they used pebbles, and from this comes the word al-ihsa' (enumeration).

Meaning: alone, with no family, children, or supporters with him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children. For every man among them, that Day, there will be a matter that will occupy him﴾ (Surah Abasa). So each one is preoccupied with his own state, oblivious to those nearest to him: ﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed﴾ (Surah al-Hajj).

And reflect on His saying: ﴿coming to Him﴾ (Surah Maryam). The servant is the one who comes by himself, choosing, and is not brought. It is as if all of them are bound to a known appointed time, and when it comes, they all hasten willingly to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 96:

Wudd (ودّ): affection and love that rests upon faith and leads to intense attachment. Al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, has placed in His creation means (asbab) for this love and affection. For example, you see a person who loves you and shows you affection: whenever you see him coming toward you, you stand up for him, greet him with a cheerful face, make room for him in the gathering, ask about him if he is absent, visit him if he is ill, share his joys, console him in his sorrows, and support him in hardships. This affection arises from a prior love and affection.

Affection may also arise because of kinship, mutual interests, or friendship. These are the causes of affection in this world among all creatures, both believers and disbelievers. But here: ﴿Surely the Most Merciful will bring about for them affection﴾ (Surah Maryam): 96.

That is: without any of these causes of affection. It is affection without kinship, without shared interests or friendship. This affection exists among those who believe. You may see a person for the first time and feel at ease with him as though you have known him, and you say to him: "I love you for the sake of God."

This is a love that God has placed among the believers, as a bounty from Him, glorified is He, and an act of generosity, not because of any of the well-known causes of affection.

Therefore Harim ibn Hayyan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, sees His servant, the believer, turn to Him with his heart, and He dwells in it, removes from his heart other than Him, and entrusts his heart, which is the most precious thing he possesses, the repository of beliefs and the spring of good deeds, and offers it to his Lord, He opens for him the hearts of all the believers.

As came in the sacred hadith: "Whenever a servant turns to Me with his heart, I turn to him with the hearts of all the believers." That is: with affection and mercy, without causes.

And in the sacred hadith: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls out in the heavens: 'Indeed I love so-and-so, so love him.' And Jibril calls out on the earth: 'Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.' And acceptance is placed for him on the earth."

So everyone who sees him loves him, as a gift and bounty from Allah, without any of the causes of affection. And although you have given to Allah, may He be exalted, what you possess, which is your heart, the repository of beliefs and the spring of all good deeds, He, may He be exalted, has granted you what He possesses of the hearts of all people, and they are in His hand, He directs them as He wills.

Our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, has taught us in His words: ﴿And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it, or return it﴾ (Surah al-Nisa'): 86.

That we should repay a favour with something better than it, and if we cannot give better, then at least return it in kind. If this is the giving of the servant, then what of the giving of the Lord?

Help (al-'awn) requires a helper (mu'in) and one who is helped (mu'an), and the helper must be stronger than the one helped, so that he bestows upon him from his surplus: health, power, wealth, or knowledge. A servant's help to his brother is limited by his abilities and capacities, but Allah's help to His servant is unlimited, because it matches the power and capacities of al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He.

Thus our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, has accustomed us that when we sacrifice a little, He gives us much without limit, as a bounty and generosity from Allah. Have you not seen that a good deed with Him, exalted is He, is rewarded tenfold, and multiplied up to seven hundred times? Is this not a profitable trade with Allah, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, shall I direct you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ (Surah al-Saff): 10.

And He said of it: ﴿A trade that will never perish﴾ (Surah Fatir): 29.
