It is as if al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, wants from us the mutual love that binds our hearts and unites us, and then He, glorified is He, grants us the price.

So: the act of faith should not be thought of as altruism; rather, faith is self-interest (atharah), and when you give charity, you are in fact seeking what is with Allah of multiplied reward. Faith, then, is a lofty form of self-regard. Yet al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, wants us to benefit others with the surplus of what we possess, as came in the hadith: "Whoever has surplus wealth, let him give it to the one who has no wealth..."

And know that Allah will compensate you with something better than what you have given. An example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness: suppose you have two sons, and you give each of them his allowance. The first used his to buy sweets, ate some of them, and gave some to his friends, while the other squandered his allowance on useless toys or the like. Which of them would you give more to afterward? In the same way, al-Haqq, glorified is He, deals with us.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 19, verse 97:

The fa' here indicates the sequencing of one thing after another, so look at the clause that follows it for this sequence. The meaning is: "Give good tidings to the God-conscious (al-muttaqin), and warn the stubborn people (al-qawm al-lud), for We have made the Qur'an easy for you."

"Yassarna al-Qur'an" (We have made the Qur'an easy): that is, We have made it subservient to you in memorization, recitation and conveying its meanings, so you deploy it in the mission for which it was revealed. The facilitation of the Qur'an is mentioned in many verses, such as the saying of the Exalted in Surah al-Qamar: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ (Surah al-Qamar, 17).

Whoever reflects on the facilitation of the Qur'an will find wonders in its style. You see a verse come in one surah with one wording, and come in the same context in another surah with a different wording. So the matter is not, then, a fixed "cliché" (ashlih thabit), nor a deaf mechanical process; it is the speech of the Lord.

Take as an example the saying of the Exalted: ﴿No! Indeed it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it.﴾ (Surah al-Muddaththir, 54-55).

And in another verse: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.﴾ (Surah al-Insan, 29).

Once He says: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder..﴾ (Surah al-Insan, 29).

And once He says: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾ (Surah Maryam, 11)... 

Here we stand before a subtle observation in Surah al-Rahman, where the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 46).

Then the discussion of them comes: in them is such-and-such, in them is such-and-such, until He reaches the restrainers of the gaze, and says: ﴿In them are restrainers of the gaze..﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 56).

Likewise in: ﴿And besides them are two gardens﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 62): in them is such-and-such, and in them is such-and-such, until He reaches the dark-eyed maidens (al-hur al-'in), and says: ﴿In them are good, beautiful ones﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 70).

You may ask: the discussion here is about the two gardens, so why does the context shift from "fihima" (in them, dual) to "fihinna" (in them, feminine plural) in this particular blessing?

They said: because the bliss of Paradise is shared, something everyone may share, except the blessing of the dark-eyed maidens, which has its own particularity. It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted, respects the feelings of jealousy in a man. In this matter each of us has his own garden, which no one else shares with him.

Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the Garden, he saw in it a palace and turned away from it. When he was asked about that, he (ﷺ) said: "It belonged to 'Umar, and I know the jealousy of 'Umar."

To this degree is the jealousy of the believer, and to this degree is the precision of expression in the Noble Qur'an.

Had Allah not revealed the Qur'an and made it easy, no one would have memorized it. The Prophet (ﷺ) would receive the verses, and when the revelation left him he would dictate them to the Companions, and keep reciting them just as they were. Had Allah not said to him: ﴿We will make you recite, so you will not forget﴾ (Surah al-A'la, 6), that would not have been made easy for him.

In our memorization of the Book of Allah we also find wonders. A child of seven can memorize the Qur'an and perfect its recitation (tajwid), and if he neglects it afterwards it slips from him, unlike a text of any other kind learned at that age, which remains stuck in his mind.

So the matter of memorizing the Qur'an is not merely a feat of retentive memory, but the help of the One who preserves it. If you remain in affection and familiarity with the Book of Allah, it stays with you; if you abandon it and neglect it, it slips away from you, as the noble hadith says: "Keep attending to the Qur'an, for by Him in whose hand my soul is, it is more prone to escape than camels in their tethers."

That is because the letters of the Qur'an are not merely letters having a written form and a spoken sound; the letters of the Qur'an are angels who line up, so they form a word, and form a verse. If you love the letter, and love the word and the verse, the angels love you, and they are arranged when you recite.

Among the wonders of the facilitation of memorizing the Qur'an is that if you apply your mind to the Qur'an and try to analyze it, you will stumble in it and make mistakes; but if you repeat the recitation just as you memorized it, by natural disposition (ala al-salīqa), the verses follow you in sequence and comply with you.

And you notice here that the Qur'an did not come with the explicit noun, but came with the pronoun of the third person in "yassarnāhu" (Surah Maryam, 97). This is because the hā' here can only refer to the Qur'an, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ (Surah al-Ikhlas, 1), where the third-person pronoun can only refer to Allah, the Exalted. And His saying: ﴿in your tongue﴾ (Surah Maryam, 97): that is, in your language, so We made it an Arabic Qur'an for an Arab people, that they might understand from you the conveying of Allah's message in good tidings and warning. Had it come to them in another language, they would have said, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿Had We made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why have its verses not been explained? What, a non-Arabic (recitation) and an Arab?"﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 44).

And the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted: ﴿and warn with it a stubborn people﴾ (Surah Maryam, 97).

Al-indhar (warning): cautioning against an evil that will occur in the future. Al-lidad (stubbornness): the violence of dispute and the fierceness of enmity. One says: "So-and-so has lidad", meaning he exaggerates in dispute, does not submit to proof or persuasion, and however much you try with him, he insists on his contention.

Almighty Allah consoles His Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم (ﷺ) for the hardship he meets in the course of his call, as if He were saying to him: Beware lest the hatred of the people for you and their aversion to the method of Allah affect you; beware lest you shrink before their tyranny in their obstinacy. These people are no mightier than their predecessors among the deniers, whom Allah destroyed. He has only let these remain because they have a mission with you.

We have already explained that some of the disbelievers who escaped being killed in some of the battles, and whose survival grieved the Muslims, later included Khalid ibn al-Walid, the Drawn Sword of Allah (sayf Allah al-maslul).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them?﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:98). Kam (how many) is an expression (khabariyyah) indicating abundance; qarn (generation) means a nation.

﴿Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a whisper?﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:98). That is, because We seized them and left no trace of them that could be perceived.

The means of perception, as is well known, are: the eye for sight, the ear for hearing, the nose for smell, the tongue for taste, and the hand for touch. By whichever instrument of perception you seek them, you will find no trace of them. As for His words, ﴿or hear from them a whisper?﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:98): ruzz (rikz) is a faint sound that you can barely hear.

This is Allah's way with the deniers of earlier nations, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Are they better than the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them, for they were criminals.﴾ (Surah al-Dukhan 44:37).

Where are ʿAd and Thamud and Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the lands? And where is Pharaoh of the stakes? Every tyrant, however high his civilization, could not preserve it, because Allah the Exalted willed that it should pass away. Are the disbelievers of Makkah mightier than all these?

Therefore, when you hear this question: ﴿Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a whisper?﴾ (Surah Maryam 19:98), you cannot but answer: I perceive none of them, and I hear no whisper from them.
